When you commit yourself to staying centered and letting go of ego, the ego will resist, and that is absolutely part of the process. You have to understand that your mind has been storing impressions, emotions, and experiences your entire life. These are not just passing thoughts; they are deeply ingrained



patterns, and when something triggers them, they will surface with full force. The mind will start talking, spinning stories, and before you know it, you’re caught. That’s just how it works. But here’s the key: over time, if you keep letting go, this reaction will lose its power.

You don’t get to choose whether something hits you or not. It’s going to happen. A situation, a word, a look from someone—it will trigger something inside, and suddenly, your mind is throwing thoughts all over the place. You don’t need to pretend it’s not happening, and you don’t need to judge yourself for it. Just don’t resist. Don’t get lost in thinking, Why is this happening? Why is this still here? It’s there because it’s inside of you, and that’s okay. The goal is not to stop things from coming up. The goal is to get so good at letting go that they no longer control you.

When the mind starts talking and emotions start flooding in, don’t fight with them—just relax behind them. If you get caught, you’re caught. Fine. Just do your best. Don’t use that as an excuse to indulge in negativity, like thinking you should be past all this already. If you fall down, just get back up. Each time you do, you will become stronger.

At some point, you will start to see that these moments, the very ones that used to take you down, are actually opportunities. They are the doorways to freedom. Every time something hits you and you choose to let go instead of resist, you become a little lighter. You become a little freer. One day, you’ll notice that what used to knock you over barely even moves you anymore. That is the beauty of this path: you just stay with it. Let go when you can, accept when you can’t, and keep on going.

10-4.q: How do I maintain a high state when I feel like I’m backsliding?
10-4.a:
When you feel like you’re backsliding, the first thing to do is change the way you’re looking at it. Stop thinking that staying in a high state is good and coming down is bad. That’s not how this works. Growth isn’t about holding on to a state—it’s about letting go of whatever is still in you that pulls you down. If something inside you is getting hit, that means there’s something left to work through. That’s a gift, not a problem. Instead of resisting it, welcome it. Let it come up, see it clearly, and use that moment to relax and let go.

You have to understand that spiritual growth isn’t about clinging to highs; it’s about removing the barriers that keep you from naturally staying there. If you truly want to be free, then every time life hits your stuff, use that as an opportunity to let go of what’s holding you down. This is why the great masters talk about surrender. The highest beings don’t go around thinking, Am I maintaining a high state? They’re just free. They’ve let go of everything that would have pulled them out of that freedom.

Look at it this way: A hot air balloon naturally rises, but if it’s tied down, it can’t go anywhere. You’re that balloon, and your old fears, reactions, and attachments are the ropes holding you down. Those ropes are very important to your growth—they are showing you exactly what’s left to let go of. You should thank them for being there, because once you deal with them, you’ll go even higher.

When you feel like you’re falling, neither get into it nor resist it. Embrace it. Worship it. Love that life is giving you this opportunity to grow. The real question isn’t “How do I stay up?” It’s “What inside of me is still pulling me down?” When you stop fighting with life and start using it to release what’s left inside of you, you’ll no longer have to try to stay high. You’ll just naturally be there because there will be nothing left to pull you out.

10-5.q: How can I stay committed to my spiritual growth despite setbacks?
10-5.a:
The first thing you need to understand is that you’re not here to achieve spiritual growth like it’s some kind of goal you check off a list. You’re here to let go of the false self that keeps you from experiencing the truth of what you are. The process of life is designed to evolve you, to break down the barriers that keep you limited. When challenges arise, they are not obstacles to your growth—they are your growth. If you can approach them with openness instead of resistance, you’ll find that the very things you once saw as setbacks were actually life perfectly guiding you toward deeper surrender.

If you make spirituality about becoming something, proving yourself, or being good enough—you will struggle. That’s the mind playing games, telling you that you need to accomplish something to be okay inside. Your life does not become meaningful because of what you do. Your life becomes meaningful when you finally realize who you truly are. This can only happen when you let go of who you are not—the identification with the made-up self-concept.

Stop trying to force your way through obstacles, and instead, surrender to them. Let them show you what you need to release. The universe is not asking you to be perfect; it’s asking you to let go. As you do, everything will unfold exactly as it needs to. The right lessons, the right people, the right opportunities will come. Your job is not to control any of it. Your job is to stay open and trust the process of life.

10-6.q: How do I handle difficult situations and let go when I’m overwhelmed?
10-6.a:
When you find yourself in the midst of a difficult situation and are struggling to let go, understand that the real work should have started long before that moment. It’s like asking, “What do I do now that my body is sick and breaking down?” when you haven’t taken care of it for years. Of course, there will be things you can do now, but the most powerful approach would have been to build strength and resilience when things weren’t so bad. If you work on staying centered with the little things in your daily life—such as traffic, the weather, or minor frustrations—then, when life throws you something big, you’ll already have the tools to handle it.

If you haven’t done that work and now you’re in the storm, the first thing you can do is recognize that everything passes. Every single moment of your life has come and gone, hasn’t it? This too shall pass. Instead of fighting the situation or getting lost in it, try looking past it. Ask yourself, “What if I could handle this? How much stronger, how much freer would I be on the other side?” Make the situation your teacher. Use it as an opportunity to grow rather than as something to resist.

The highest approach isn’t about trying to control the situation—it’s about working with yourself. You can use mantra, you can shift your focus, but ultimately, you need to recognize that the worst things that have ever happened to you are often the best for your growth. They push you to grow in ways you would not have otherwise. You might not see it now, but one day, you’ll look back and realize that the challenges shaped you, deepened you, and took you places you never would have imagined.

Life can play hardball, and if you resist, you’ll suffer. But if you embrace what’s happening and allow life to teach you instead of fighting against it, you’ll discover something incredible: no matter what happens, you’re okay. When you truly understand this, life ceases to be something you’re trying to get through—it becomes something you’re willing to fully embrace with an open heart.

10-7.q: If I want to grow spiritually, how do I maintain awareness during overwhelming events like fear or crises?
10-7.a:
When you go through a period of life when everything is fine, it’s relatively easy to stay centered. But when something happens that is big enough to shake you, the mind goes crazy, fear escalates, and you feel completely thrown off. In those moments, it feels impossible to stay present in the seat of awareness. So what do you do?

First, understand that you are not enlightened yet—there’s still plenty of evolution ahead of you. When powerful events occur, they show where you are in your spiritual growth. This is true for both positive and negative experiences. An overwhelming desire can arise out of nowhere, just as powerfully as an overwhelming sense of fear. They are both the same principle: an inner experience gets so big that it pulls you out of your center. Spiritual practices are about preparing for these events before they happen. Learn to stay conscious now, before the storm comes. The more you practice staying centered in your everyday life, the less likely the bigger challenges will throw you.

Let’s say something happens, and you get pulled out of your center. What now? Don’t resist, don’t rationalize, don’t make excuses—just come back. The moment you become aware that you’ve lost yourself in fear, come back as soon as you can. No judgment. No guilt. Just return. If you practice this, over time you’ll find that you stay centered longer before getting lost, and you return more quickly after the fall. That’s evolution.

When you do come back from a fall, don’t store the experience as something negative. That’s how people become afraid of growthful experiences. Instead, say thank you. Thank you for the opportunity to grow. This is how life’s experiences help you evolve. Every difficult moment is an opportunity to grow beyond yourself. Just always do your best at your current level of evolution, and the amazing process of life will take you to the next level.

10-8.q: I am letting go of thoughts and emotions so they can pass through, but I’m experiencing overwhelming fatigue and heaviness, rather than clarity. Should I continue to stay centered and allow the energies to pass through, or is a different approach needed?
10-8.a:
There are many stages you go through during your inner growth. You will have times when the energy feels high and clear, and there will be times when you feel you have no energy at all. The heaviness and lack of energy are simply signs of a blockage, and that blockage will release over time if you continue to let go. You are correct that regardless of how the energy is flowing or not flowing, your work is to stay centered in the Self, relax and release, and simply be aware of the energy passing through. That is your inner work.

However, that is not your outer work. As much as possible, you want to set patterns in your daily life that support your inner growth and a sense of consistent outer stability. Your daily routines are very important. It is very hard to stay on course and not let the dips and changes in your energy flow dictate your actions in life. But if you are going through a time when your energy is low and you feel you can barely move, you should still try go about your normal daily life to the very best of your ability.

For example, if you have a job, you go to work and do the very best that you can while you are inwardly letting go. Don’t worry that the best you can do when you are feeling low is not as good as the best you can do when you are feeling clear and high. That is not what matters—what matters is that you did the very best you could. The results of the best you can do are always honorable. In addition, by looking past your inner disturbance and simply focusing on your work, you’ll find that the period of low energy will pass more quickly, and you won’t dip as low. If you approach your life in this way, you will find that your daily activities are actually an important part of the grace that carries you through tough times.

10-9.q: Is it normal to feel discomfort or low energy levels when going through spiritual growth?
10-9.a:
What you’re experiencing is not only normal—it’s beautiful. When you sincerely ask, “Who am I?” you’re turning your awareness inward, and that begins to stir things up inside. You may start to feel discomforts you never felt before. That’s because you’re opening. As you open, the stored blockages inside you—your past experiences, your unresolved emotions, all the impressions you’ve accumulated—start to rise up. They were always there, but now that you’re turning inward, you’re becoming aware of them.

This is not something to be afraid of. It’s actually a deep cleansing. Think of it like a pool where dirt and debris have settled at the bottom. On the surface, the water looks clear, but when you start stirring it, all that muck rises up. That’s what’s happening inside of you. When you stop distracting yourself with the outside world and turn your attention inward, all the stuff you’ve suppressed begins to come up so it can pass through. But instead of letting it go, most people get involved—they resist it, they fight it, and that’s what causes suffering.

The key is to welcome the process—it’s called spiritual cleansing. If you were in India, you might climb the Himalayas and seek out a master just to receive a touch that would initiate this exact cleansing process. Instead, life is giving it to you naturally. Don’t resist it. When you feel discomfort, don’t pull away—relax and let it pass through. It’s just like a mother in labor—screaming in pain, yet willing to go through the process because she knows she’s giving birth to something beautiful. That’s what’s happening to you. You’re giving birth to your soul.

Don’t pray for the cleansing to stop—pray for the blockages to be released. Offer them up to the Universe and say, “Take it. I don’t want this inside me anymore.” You don’t want to carry around all this stored pain, these blockages that keep you from being open and filled with love. Let go, and what you’ll find is that beneath all of it, there’s nothing but joy, light, and peace. It’s already there—you just have to clear out what’s blocking it.

10-10.q: How does setting boundaries affect spiritual growth?
10-10.a:
When you talk about boundaries in the context of spiritual growth and acceptance, you have to be very careful. Why? Because when you set a boundary, what you’re really saying is, “I can’t handle this.” That is exactly the opposite of growth. Spiritual growth is expanding your ability to remain open in the face of life’s experiences. Life is not something you get to control by drawing lines around what you will and won’t accept. Life just happens—things come and go, events unfold, and your job is to remain open and allow those experiences to help you grow.

This doesn’t mean you just sit there passively allowing people to mistreat you. Surrender doesn’t mean you don’t take action—it means you don’t take action out of reactivity. You don’t set boundaries because you’re afraid or because you can’t handle something. Instead, you step back, let go of your initial reactions, and ask yourself, Am I seeing this clearly? So much of what people call boundaries is just projection—reacting to past pain and imposing that reaction onto present situations. If you had a bad experience at a job before, you might walk into the next one already convinced the same thing is going to happen. That’s not clarity—that’s carrying your past into the present.

Acceptance means staying quiet for a moment and watching your inner reaction to the situation. Once you’ve settled yourself, ask, Is this actually happening the way I think it is? If so, what is the appropriate response? That’s very different from saying, “I have a boundary, and I refuse to deal with this.” When you accept reality and seek to respond appropriately, you’re not running away, and you’re not avoiding. You’re handling life with clarity. If someone is mistreating you, you don’t just sit there and let it happen—but you also don’t run away out of fear. You handle it but from a place of strength, not weakness.

For example, if someone steals your car, you don’t just sit there and say, “Oh well, I accept it.” No, you surrender the part of you that’s freaking out because you can’t handle it, and then you take action. You call the police. You call your insurance company. You do what needs to be done, but you don’t react from a place of panic or resistance. Because life doesn’t have boundaries, it does all kinds of things. Your growth is about expanding your capacity to stay open while life moves through you. Then you take appropriate action when needed—without making the mistake of believing that you have to protect yourself from life. If you act from clarity instead of fear, you’re not setting boundaries—you’re just dealing with life in an impersonal, appropriate manner. That’s real spiritual growth.

11-1.q: I have had a problem with fear since I was a child. How do I work with it in a compassionate way?
11-1.a:
An important part of your spiritual growth is learning how to work through past experiences that have left you feeling fear. The path of letting go is never about heartlessly abandoning that scared part of your psyche. True spiritual growth is about being willing to experience fear when it comes up but remaining centered enough to work with it so that it is not controlling your life.

Your ability to work with fear comes in very distinct steps. To begin with, you must learn to immediately relax the moment you start to feel the vibration of fear. Relax your shoulders, chest, belly, and buttocks instead of tightening up in resistance to the experience. Start with the very small expressions of fear within you. Perhaps someone is passing you while you’re driving, and you see yourself starting to tense up. Or maybe your mind is bothering you about something minor you said during a passing conversation with a friend. There are lots of these moments during the day that are not actually threatening, but you still feel some fear come up. Dare to relax instead of resist. Let the initial impulse of fear pass through. You don’t need to protect yourself from these reactions of fear; they are not really threatening you.

Over time, if you can stay centered in the face of these minor fears, the scared part of your being will begin to see that the current reality is not as threatening as it thought. That habitually scared part of your being will begin to feel comfortable that you, your higher consciousness, are there to help it through these moments. You are not alone—the higher part of your being is there to raise the lower part.

When you reach this stage, you are not denying the fear or even trying to get rid of it. You are simply remaining in witness consciousness and allowing the fearful energy from the past to pass through. As you practice relaxing through minor fears, you are actually learning how to deal with fear itself. You will find that remaining in witness consciousness becomes your natural state. Once you can relax through the initial impulse of fear, you can interact with the world from a much deeper place. You can now actually deal with the outer situation, instead of having to deal with your inner fears about it. Without realizing it, you have used the impulse of fear to help you grow spiritually. There is now less fear and more centered consciousness. Letting go is a very beautiful practice that can transmute lower self into higher self.

11-2.q: I’ve always had a very deep fear of injury and death. I’ve tried relaxing and releasing it, but it keeps coming back. How do I deal with this fear?
11-2.a:
Fear can be very strong and sometimes even overwhelming. But never forget you are not the fear; you are the consciousness that is aware of the fear. The nature of consciousness is joy, love, and absolute well-being. But since consciousness is now focusing on fear, it is experiencing the fear it is focusing on. Don’t fight the fear, and don’t be afraid of the fear. Just know it as part of human nature. Relax around it, honor its right to be, but don’t get lost in it. Let it pass by, the way a matador steps aside and lets the charging bull pass right by. Don’t touch the fear; work to shift your awareness off the fear. That is why people do mantra—to focus on something other than the disturbances created by the mind and heart. Don’t push the fear away; don’t suppress it. Simply shift your consciousness onto something else. If the fear keeps pulling you back into it, don’t fight it—just relax and actively welcome it to release and pass through you. It’s just energy trying to release. Your only job is to help it.

If remaining centered in the face of fear seems impossible, I will give you a technique I used in the early years of my growth. Instead of trying to stay above the fear as it passes through you, there is a very sacred place inside of you where you can lay down very quietly and allow the fear to pass over you. This requires no will or strength; it is an act of complete surrender to the experience. Try lying down on your back with your arms out to your sides. Relax so much that you feel like you are melting into the floor. Focus on the feeling of melting backward into that space, instead of focusing on the fear that is blowing like wind over you. You are safe there and can weather the storm. This will allow the energy of fear to release without you reacting in resistance.

People don’t know how to release like this because they were never taught how. Instead, they try to change things outside so they don’t have to handle the inner fear. The fear never really goes away that way. It will always come back. If you learn to relax in the face of the fear, you can learn to let the root cause of the fear surface and pass through.

Always remember: that which is aware of the fear is a billion times more powerful than the fear itself.

11-3.q: What is the relationship between our fears and our preferences?
11-3.a:
There is a powerful relationship between fear and preferences. When you prefer something to be a certain way, you naturally experience fear at the possibility it won’t turn out that way. The deeper the preference, the stronger the fear. This isn’t about instinctual fear—the biological kind that protects the body from danger. That’s natural, and it’s there for survival. If a tiger is chasing you, you should be afraid. That fear is not the problem.

The fear we’re talking about is psychological fear. The “what-ifs.” What if they don’t like me? What if I fail? What if my feelings get hurt? Fears such as these come from your mind spinning stories about how things need to be for you to be okay. You’re afraid because you have an expectation, a preference for things being a certain way. If you didn’t have that preference, there wouldn’t be fear. Imagine you didn’t care what people think of you—then you wouldn’t be afraid of being judged. Imagine you didn’t need to be in control—then you wouldn’t be afraid of uncertainty. Fear is the tension you feel when your preferences might not be met.

From a spiritual growth point of view, you don’t allow the fear to pull you into it; you allow it to come up and pass through you. You never fight or suppress fear, either. Instead, you recognize it for what it is: blocked energy inside of you. That fear is showing you where you’re holding on to unresolved blockages from the past. If you allow yourself to relax and not resist, something amazing happens. You start to let go. The preference loses its grip on you. The fear dissolves on its own, because it only existed in relation to your attachment.

This doesn’t mean you force yourself to have no preferences. That’s not how it works. Preferences naturally fall away as your inner blockages dissolve. You don’t have to push them away; they just stop controlling you. Maybe once you failed in a math class and were embarrassed because you had tied your self-worth to being good at math. As you grow and release those old wounds, you stop caring. You realize your worth was never tied to that. Suddenly, the fear is gone. This is how fear fades—not by force, but by letting go of what created it in the first place. You must work at the root cause.

Eventually, you will realize that it is not the situation itself that is causing fear—it’s your need for things to be a certain way that generates mental and emotional disturbance. When you stop committing your life to your preferences, you will become free of these fears. They will no longer have a hold on you, and you will be free to openly experience every moment of your life.

11-4.q: I was diagnosed with a serious illness, aggressive cancer, and the probability of recurrence is very high. How can I stay in witness consciousness and use this for my spiritual growth?
11-4.a:
I am so sorry to hear of your serious illness. There are so many levels at which your question can be answered. They all include compassion, but one response can actually make a huge difference in how you live the remaining years of your life. The problem is that most people are not receptive to the deepest and surest way to work with life’s issues. If you fear a recurrence of the cancer and the possibility of an early death, it’ll be pretty much impossible to enjoy the remaining years of your life. The best you’ll be able to do is suppress your underlying fears, and that does not lead to a life of openness and appreciation.

What you must do, if you are willing to try, is to change your entire attitude about your remaining years. Start with the affirmation that everyone dies; in fact, everything that was ever born is going to die. How long a person lives is not the important part—it’s the joy, love, and pure appreciation for each day that makes the next day worth living. Don’t worry about how many years you have left—learn to appreciate each day, one at a time. This is all done by working with your thoughts.

Of course, by default, we don’t tend to think this way. It may be challenging to do so, but you can work at making that change in your thinking. Use an affirmation, like: I am grateful for the day I have been given, and I will use every moment of it to love everyone and everything that unfolds before me. If I get one more day—that is a treasure chest of experiences I get to have. Work on thinking like this. Don’t be mad at God or the Universe for your illness; be grateful that you have one more day to live fully and love openly. Reread the chapter “Contemplating Death” in The Untethered Soul. Work on this, and everything will look different. You will be a light of inspiration to all those around you.

11-5.q: Recently I started experiencing a lot of fear and anxiety when I try to let go of the ego. I am concerned I will become nothing. Is this the ego trying to hold on to its false self-concept?
11-5.a:
Sometimes when you are going through deep growth, the lower self becomes frightened and challenged. It is really important to let go and not listen to it. At the same time, it is important to be kind and not push the fear down or push the lower self into a corner inside yourself. Be kind to yourself. You can use loving affirmations, if it helps. This could be as simple as saying I am always okay or I am always loved. Allow yourself to feel that loving presence.

This is how you deal with fear in the short term.

Over time, as you continue to let go and fall back into your true Self (the conscious awareness), you’ll find the fear you have of losing yourself will go away. The more you experience your deeper presence by simply watching your mind and heart, the more you’ll see that your true being is ever-present and unchanging. Your awareness does not leave; it is just the noise of the personal mind and heart that leaves. It’s a very natural process. As the lower self thins out, all the energy that was creating it comes back to your center. You’ll find that the lower energy is naturally replaced with a happy, loving sense of presence and fulfillment.

So, in truth, you are not losing yourself—you are actually finding yourself. You will begin to experience a fullness, like everything and everyone is a part of you. They say that in the end, you do not become nothing—you actually become everything!

11-6.q: How do you overcome fear, such as fear of pain before a necessary medical procedure?
11-6.a:
When you’re dealing with the fear of pain from an upcoming event, such as a necessary medical procedure, you have to start by being completely honest with yourself. Ask yourself, Do I have to go through this procedure? Yes or no? If the answer is no, then don’t do it. If the answer is yes—if you’ve done the cost-benefit analysis, consulted the experts, and made the decision that this is the right thing for your well-being—then that part is settled. You’re not going to keep going back and forth in your mind, questioning it over and over. That only feeds the fear. Instead, you see reality, make a decision, and say to yourself, This is happening, and I am doing this. That clarity is powerful. It stops you from letting your mind play games with you.

Once you’ve accepted the reality of the situation, you shift your focus. Instead of obsessing over your fear, you start to reframe the experience. You tell yourself, I really want to do this. I’m looking forward to getting through it so I can be on the other side. You use affirmations. You remind yourself, I can’t wait for this to be done. Imagine how much better I’ll feel knowing it’s behind me. I’m taking care of myself. I’m doing the right thing. At first, you may not fully believe what you’re saying, but that doesn’t matter. You keep saying it anyway. You give your mind something positive to focus on, an alternative to sitting in fear.

One of the best ways to handle fear is to mentally skip past the part you’re dreading. Don’t fixate on the procedure itself—jump beyond it. Imagine yourself afterward, relieved, free of worry, stronger for having faced it. Your mind is going to make up stories anyway, so why not choose a story that serves you? Instead of picturing fear and pain, picture yourself on the other side, looking back and saying, “That wasn’t so bad. I did it. It’s done.” That shift in perspective changes everything.

Understand this: You have to be willing to make this mental shift—it won’t just happen on its own. Fear will keep pulling you down unless you actively lift yourself up. Take responsibility for where you place your attention. Instead of letting fear drag you into suffering, guide yourself toward a place of strength. This is something you can do, and once you start, you’ll realize you’re more capable than you ever thought.

11-7.q: I fear major life tragedies like losing a child, getting a terminal illness, or experiencing a disaster. How does surrender work when someone is experiencing extreme tragedy and pain?
11-7.a:
Undoubtedly, there are horrific events that take place on this planet. The question is, can you handle that? This is an especially poignant question if you have fear of events that are not actually happening to you. If you live your life driven by fears that something bad might happen, you will live a life of constant suffering. It might as well be happening because it’s causing you constant pain. The good news is that in this situation, you have complete control. You are the one who is allowing your mind to fixate on something that is not real. Empower yourself to change—work on letting go of the part of you that distrusts life and thinks it is unsafe. Stop and question yourself: How many moments of your life were actually as traumatic and difficult as the scenarios you are imagining? It’s probably a very small number of moments compared to the rest of your life. Yet you still fear them.

One practice is to ask yourself regularly, Is everything okay right now? Can I handle this moment? If you keep asking this regularly, you will see that you really are okay the vast majority of the time. Take refuge in that realization. Keep relaxing and releasing each time you feel the fear, and over time, the fears will diminish.

When it comes to horrific experiences that are actually happening, people will naturally experience fear, along with the physical and emotional pain the event creates. That is part of the reality of living through such an ordeal. Surrender is not about denying the reality of these events. It is about allowing them to ultimately pass through without leaving permanent scars and fears in the psyche. Part of the process of inner healing is to fully accept that the event took place and see what you can do to view it in a positive light. Maybe the event taught you to be strong, to have a deeper understanding of humanity, or to have compassion for others who have suffered trauma. Find a way to raise yourself through the situation—you learned, you grew, you became a greater person for having lived through the experience. Yes, it brought pain, but it also expanded you and helped you evolve.

11-8.q: Is fear part of the process when deeply buried emotions begin to surface? How do I stay motivated when deep emotional cleansing feels overwhelming and regressive?
11-8.a:
When those deeply buried emotions begin to surface, yes, fear is absolutely part of the process. This fear isn’t something wrong or something to avoid— it’s a natural protective mechanism that’s been guarding these emotions for years, perhaps decades. Your psyche buried these feelings for a reason, and now they’re coming up. Fear arises to say, “Wait—are you sure you want to go there?”

What you’re experiencing during deep emotional cleansing isn’t regression—it’s progression. You’re finally allowing yourself to face what you’ve spent an enormous amount of energy avoiding. The feeling of being overwhelmed comes because you’re experiencing both the emotion itself and all the resistance you’ve built around it. When you feel like you’re drowning, remember that you are not the emotions or the fear—you’re the awareness that notices them arising within your consciousness.

Motivation does not come from fighting these emotions, but from a profound understanding that facing them is the only path to freedom. Every time you allow a buried emotion to surface without resistance, you are freeing energy that has been locked in your heart. This is spiritual work of the highest order. The temporary discomfort you feel is the price of permanent liberation. When you’re in the thick of it and feeling overwhelmed, remind yourself that millions of people live their entire lives avoiding this work, carrying these burdens to their graves. You’ve already chosen the path of freedom—now honor your courage by continuing.

The key is to relax in the face of your resistance. When fear arises, don’t push against it or analyze it. Simply notice it, relax your shoulders, open your heart, and breathe. Let it pass through you like a storm cloud passing through the sky. The sky itself remains untouched. This is the practice: to witness without clinging; to feel without identifying. Your awareness is vast enough to hold any emotion that arises.

Remember, this cleansing isn’t something you’re doing—it’s something you’re allowing. The natural state of your being is joy, peace, and love. Suppressed emotions are coming up precisely because they’re ready to be released. Trust this process. Trust that the intelligence that created the universe is perfectly capable of healing your heart—if only you’ll step aside and allow it to work through you.

In the end, staying motivated is about remembering what’s on the other side: a life of openness, freedom, and unconditional joy. Each emotion you face and release is a step toward living untethered from the patterns of your past. This work isn’t easy, but nothing of true value ever is. Keep going. The light you seek is not somewhere in the distance—it’s what remains when you’ve allowed the darkness to pass through.

Karma, Free Will, and the Law of Attrac.name: Karma, Free Will, and  the Law of Attraction

12-1.q: What is the role of free will in dealing with the world, emotions, and thoughts?
12-1.a:
The role of free will in dealing with the outer world and your inner state is simple, yet profound. You have a choice every moment: to accept or resist. That is the only real control you have. Life will bring you experiences—some beautiful, some difficult. Your freedom lies in how you handle those experiences. If you choose acceptance, you are allowing life to flow through you. You don’t get caught struggling with life; you remain centered in the seat of Self. If you resist, if you push against what is happening, you create tension, turmoil, and suffering within yourself.

This is where free will meets the spiritual path—it’s at the point of acceptance versus resistance. Every time something happens outside, every time a thought arises or an emotion stirs inside you, you have the opportunity to choose: Do you open, or do you close? Do you allow the energy to move through, or do you fight with it? If you resist, you don’t just resist the situation; you resist the natural flow of life itself. You hold on to pain, you create blockages, and then you have to deal with all of that. If you surrender, if you accept what is given, you stay open and free to interact from a place of clarity. Ultimately, that openness pulls you back into alignment with something much greater than yourself.

Look at the highest teachings—this is what they’ve always shown us. Even in the most difficult moments, there is a choice: resistance or surrender. Even Christ himself, when faced with the ultimate challenge, said, May this cup pass from me—but then, Not my will, but Thy will be done. That is the choice. It’s not about making life go your way. It’s not about controlling every thought and every feeling. It’s about letting go, trusting, and allowing life to unfold as it is meant to. That is the highest use of your will: to surrender to what is and stay open no matter what.

If people truly understood this and lived it, the world would be a very different place. Resistance is what causes division, pain, and suffering. When you surrender, you find peace—not because life is perfect, but because you are no longer fighting it. You have free will—learn to use it wisely. Don’t use it to control the world or fight with your mind; use it to stay open, to accept, and to allow life to take you exactly where you are meant to go.

12-2.q: How do your teachings view karma, and how can one let go of it?
12-2.a:
If you’re carrying the idea that karma is some external force dictating your life, let that go. Karma is not some cosmic punishment system—it’s just the energy you hold inside yourself from the past, attracting present events. If you have unresolved emotions, attachments, or regrets, those stay inside of you. Because they’re inside of you, they continue to shape your experiences in life. The external world isn’t keeping that karma alive—you are. If you want to be free of karma, you don’t need to perform rituals, seek forgiveness from some higher authority, or try to pay it off. You simply need to let go of what you’re holding on to inside.

If you did something in the past that you now regret, it can still weigh on you. That weight is your karma. It’s not about what happened—it’s about



the fact that you are still carrying it. The key isn’t to suppress it, deny it, or justify it. You just have to let it move through you. True remorse is not guilt or shame. It’s a deep recognition that, given who you are now, you would not act the same way again. That’s enough. The moment you fully allow that realization to pass through you—without holding on to it, without resisting it—you burn away the karma. It’s gone because you are no longer holding on to it. In a real sense, you have worked it through on the inside.

Karma is simply unfinished business. It’s the energy of your past that you haven’t let go of yet. The reason it comes back to you is because you’re still energetically tied to it. The moment you truly release it, it no longer has power over you. That’s why the great masters say that in a moment of true enlightenment, all karmic seeds are burned away. This is because in that moment, you have finally let go of your lower self, the one who created the karma in the first place.

Please don’t sit around worrying about your karma. Instead, let go of the tendencies inside you that caused it. Keep surrendering and releasing what comes up, and you will naturally rise above the part of you that has any need for lessons from the past. When that happens, you won’t have to ask how to let go of karma—you will already be free.

12-3.q: What is the connection between free will and karma?
12-3.a:
You absolutely have free will, and you are using it all the time. The question is, what are you using it for? Right now, your will is being used to stay identified with the patterns and conditioning inside of you. When a habitual reaction arises—whether it’s fear, desire, guilt, or anything else—you have the free will to engage with it or let it go. If you choose to engage with these stored patterns, that’s where the concept of karma comes in.

People say that if you use your will improperly, you take on bad karma. But karma isn’t some external force punishing you. It’s simply the consequence of expressing the energy you’ve stored inside. If you’ve built up guilt, fear, or negativity, those seeds will keep sprouting in your life. You don’t escape karma by avoiding life—you free yourself by working through what arises. If a past mistake keeps coming up in your mind, ask yourself, Would I do that again? If the answer is no, then you’ve learned your lesson. There is no need to carry it anymore. That’s how you burn karma—not by paying a price, but by evolving beyond it.

You are not here to be run by your past. You are here to use life to let go of yourself so that something greater can unfold. The moment you decide to stop clinging to old patterns, you begin to rise. As you rise, everything changes. You don’t have to fight your karma or force yourself to be free. Just step back, relax, and let go—and watch as life takes care of the rest.

12-4.q: Do you think will is an unlimited resource, or does it have a threshold?
12-4.a:
To answer this question, you first have to ask yourself—where does will come from? Will is the force created by the focusing of consciousness. When you need to do math in your head, you have to concentrate. Concentration is the willful act of focusing your awareness.

The great masters tell you that divine will is what created everything. It is the force that brought every atom into existence and holds it all together. You have access to that same consciousness, but you’re blocked by layers of personal identity formed by your past experiences. The more you stop focusing on that false identity, the more your consciousness is free to expand, and with it, your will becomes stronger and freer.

When you think your will is limited, what’s really happening is that you’ve reached the edge of what your personal self can handle. If you let go of the part of you that thinks, I can only do so much, you will see that your capacity for will is infinitely greater than you believed. The more you align with the deeper truth of who you are, the more your will is able to flow without obstruction.

Don’t think of will as something you have a little bit of and need to conserve. Recognize that will is as boundless as the consciousness from which it arises. Your job is not to strengthen it—it is to remove the blocks that keep you from experiencing it fully. Let go of yourself, and you will see there is no limit to the will within you.

12-5.q: What about the Law of Attraction? Is it a good thing to focus on?
12-5.a:
There is a truth to the Law of Attraction, but probably not in the way you think. The way you see the world is filtered through what’s going on inside of you. If you’re hungry, you notice restaurants. If you’re lonely, you notice people. If you’re afraid, you see threats everywhere. That’s not some mystical force bringing things to you—it’s just that your mind is distorting reality according to its own conditioning. In such moments, you don’t actually see the world as it is; you see it through the veil of your mind. When your mind is filled with desires, fears, and preferences, your experience of life becomes warped by all of that.

This is where you need to be careful. People love the idea that they can just decide what they want, think about it a lot, and the universe will give it to them. But how did you decide what you want? Notice that something you perceived as positive yesterday may appear as negative today. Which is it? It’s going to be based on your mind’s current and past impressions—samskaras. Do you really want to reinforce those impressions and make them the meaning of your life?

If you really want a higher way to live, forget about trying to control what comes to you. That’s just your ego playing God. Instead, let go of yourself. Let go of the need to make life into what you think it should be. The universe has been unfolding perfectly for billions of years. You just got here a few decades ago, and now you think you know how it’s supposed to go? The Tao, the natural flow of life, is already handling everything. Your job is not to tell it what to do—it’s to let go of yourself enough to come into harmony with it. Life will give you tasks to do. Just put your whole being into doing each task to the best of your ability. In other words, serve life instead of your ego. When you do that, life doesn’t just give you what you want; it gives you something far greater—what you need in order to reach unconditional well-being.

12-6.q: How can I attract the right partner to build a family once I have a vision of a perfect future?
12-6.a:
The first thing you need to understand is that if you’re thinking that life is supposed to match your vision, you’re already setting yourself up for trouble. You are creating a fixed idea of how things need to be—the perfect partner, the perfect child, the perfect future. Life doesn’t work that way. The more you insist on things being a certain way, the more suffering you will create for yourself and everyone involved. If you cling to your idea of perfection, what happens if life doesn’t unfold according to that plan? What if your partner isn’t always who you thought they would be? What if you find out you can’t have children? Are you going to be devastated? Are you going to reject life because it didn’t match your expectations? That’s not a foundation for love; that’s a foundation for suffering.

Instead of using your will to try to control how things turn out, learn to let go. Let life bring you what is meant for you. Because, in truth, you don’t know how to pick the perfect partner or force perfect outcomes years in advance. Things change, and you need to be okay, completely okay, with whatever unfolds. If challenges arise, they are there for your growth. Your job is not to dictate how life should be. Your job is to show up each day, ready and willing to serve whatever unfolds in front of you.

If you live this way, you will find yourself attracting exactly what is right for you. Not because you controlled it, but because you aligned yourself with life instead of resisting it. If life hands you something unexpected, you will meet it with grace, not disappointment. True love is not about trying to orchestrate the right conditions—it’s about being fully present, open-hearted, and ready to embrace life however it comes. The highest way to live is not to force life to match your desires, but to surrender to the flow of life and let it show you what is meant to be.

Stop trying to control everything in a relationship. Stop trying to make sure everything turns out the way you thought it would. Instead, wake up every morning, take a deep breath, and say, “I’m back. Let’s see what gifts life has in store for today.” That’s how you find true love. That’s how you live a life filled with joy and freedom.

12-7.q: Does the external world change as I grow internally?
12-7.a:
If you are growing inside, does the external world change? That’s a beautiful way to look at it, and many people teach it that way. But look deeper. What’s actually happening is not that the world outside is changing, but that you are seeing it differently. If you put on dark glasses, the world looks dark. If you put on rose-colored glasses, the world looks rosy. But if you take off the glasses altogether, you see things as they truly are. As you clean up inside, as you stop projecting your fears, desires, and disturbances onto the world, the world starts to look clearer, more harmonious. In truth, it was always like that—you were just distorting it with your own mind.

The universe is already perfect. Every star is exactly where it belongs. The sun is precisely the right distance from the earth so that life can flourish. Babies form in the womb by themselves. You didn’t do any of that. It just happens because the entire universe is unfolding exactly as it should. But when you are caught up in your personal preferences, you don’t see this perfection. You divide life into good and bad based on what suits you. If something happens that you like, you say life is working for you. If something happens that you don’t like, you think something is wrong. But what if you stopped interfering? What if you let go of yourself and simply observe reality as it is?

That’s why the great teachings don’t tell you to try to control the world so it gives you what you want. They tell you to seek something higher. Seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all things shall be added unto you. That means stop seeking for yourself first—your wants, your fears, your personal preferences—and see how life unfolds. You will find that life is always taking care of things. The forests get watered, the animals know how to feed themselves, the planets move in perfect order. None of that is because of you. It’s because life knows what it’s doing.

As you grow internally, what really happens is you stop distorting life with your personal struggles. You stop dumping your inner turmoil onto the world. When you stop interfering, life flows in ways you never imagined. But it’s not because the world is changing—it’s because you are finally seeing it clearly. The perfection was always there. Now, you’re just getting out of the way.

13-1.q: What is the best way to start letting go as a beginner in spiritual practice?
13-1.a:
The best way to start letting go is to start small. You can’t just jump into the deep end and let go of all your deepest fears and attachments overnight. That’s not how it works. You’ve spent a lifetime identifying with your thoughts, emotions, and preferences, and they feel real to you. If you try to tackle the biggest things first, you’re going to get overwhelmed. Instead, start with something simple—something that doesn’t really matter but still gets to you.

Start with the weather. Yes, the weather. It’s the perfect first teacher. Why? Because your mind does all kinds of neurotic things about it. I don’t like this rain. It’s too hot. It’s so humid. But let’s be honest—none of that changes the weather, does it? The rain isn’t falling just to annoy you. The sun isn’t shining too brightly because it’s out to get you. It’s just doing what it does. Yet you’re sitting there bothering yourself about it. That’s the key realization: the moment in front of you is not bothering you—you’re bothering yourself about the moment in front of you.

Your first practice in letting go is to stop bothering yourself about meaningless things. Make a commitment to yourself: “I will no longer bother myself about the weather.” Every time you catch yourself complaining and wishing it were different, just stop. Relax into what is. Accept it fully. Why? Because resisting it does absolutely nothing except make you suffer. That’s 100 percent cost with zero benefit. That would be a terrible business decision.

If you can train yourself to let go of something as simple as the weather, you’ll begin to understand how to do it with the bigger things in your life. First, it’s the weather. Then it’s the traffic. Then it’s what someone said to you. Eventually, it’s the deeper things—the disappointments, worries, and fears of the past, present, and future. The more you practice letting go, the more you will see that these deeper things start to fall off naturally.

13-2.q: How do I maintain my intent to relax and release when it starts to erode over time?
13-2.a:
To begin with, understand that what you’re experiencing is completely natural. Intent is not something you set once and then expect it to stay perfectly clear forever. Just like anything in life, your intent to relax and release will have its ebbs and flows. It’s not that something dramatic has to happen to make it fade—it just slowly gets clouded over by the noise of the mind and the pull of old habits. That’s why it’s essential to have regular practices that help realign you with your highest intent.

One of the simplest and most powerful things you can do is set aside dedicated time each day—morning and evening—to recommit yourself to letting go. It doesn’t have to be long. Even ten or fifteen minutes where you sit quietly, take a breath, and consciously reaffirm your commitment to letting go can make a profound difference. This practice reminds you of what you’re doing with your life and why, so you don’t drift as easily. At the end of the day, take a moment to reflect. Look at what you held on to, what you didn’t release, and see if you can let it go now. That way you don’t have to carry it forward into tomorrow.



If you make this a regular part of your life, something incredible starts to happen. Because you’re reinforcing your intent every day, you’ll find that it doesn’t erode as easily. You just naturally stay aware instead of letting unconscious tendencies take over. Over time, you’ll look back and realize that these small moments of recommitment were among the most important things you’ve done with your life. They anchored you in your practice, kept you aligned with your highest path, and ultimately transformed your entire inner experience.

So don’t worry if your intent seems to fade sometimes. That’s just life. If you honor your intent enough to renew it each day, you’ll find that it stays with you more and more. The commitment to letting go becomes second nature, and instead of losing yourself in resistance, you’ll naturally relax, release, and flow with life.

13-3.q: How can I bridge the gap between understanding spiritual teachings and living them consistently?
13-3.a:
The fact that you recognize such a gap is, in and of itself, great awareness. That’s witness consciousness: you’re already in there noticing what’s going on inside. You see the potential to live the teachings, but living them is not always easy. That’s okay, because the deeper question is, what is your intent? Do you intend to do this to the best of your ability? That’s what matters.

Your intent is everything. You don’t have to be perfect. You don’t have to get it right all the time. That’s not the point. It’s like learning to play the piano or tennis—you don’t start out playing like a master. You miss shots; you hit wrong notes. But if your intent is there, you keep going. You practice, and every time you make a mistake or fall, you get back up. You don’t quit. The real trouble isn’t in the mistakes or the falling; it’s in abandoning your intent. It’s when you say, “I can’t do this,” or “I don’t want to do this anymore,” and you turn away. That’s when you lose your way. Your intent has shifted from freedom to distraction, from growth to avoidance. You can be sure that will never work.

On the other hand, if you hold your intent and stay with it—you’re going to make it. That’s how it works. And here’s the most beautiful part: you are not doing this alone. In fact, you can’t do it alone. It’s too big. You will find that something very great is carrying you. There is a force, something invisible yet deeply real, that is helping you. And when you stay with your intent, you’ll start to notice this force. The right thing will show up at just the right time. You’ll receive exactly what you need to take the next step, to handle the next challenge. It will strengthen you, and before you know it, you’ll find yourself capable of handling what once seemed impossible.

It is true that the mind is very powerful, and the beliefs you hold shape your experience. If you believe that your heart’s natural state is disturbance, you will have to live in that disturbance. If you understand that your heart’s natural state is openness and joy, that state will always be there. We forget this because we’ve been disconnected for so long. But the moment you entertain the possibility that openness and peace are your true nature, things will start to change.

So just keep your intent. That’s all you need. Stay with it, and you will see—your sincere intent will carry you.

13-4.q: How do I handle intense emotions or energies that arise during spiritual growth?
13-4.a:
You are where you are at any given moment, and you don’t really have a choice about that. The lower self is there, and if you keep focusing on it, it will dictate your actions and your whole experience of life. It doesn’t have to stay that way. The question is, where is your polestar? Where are you aiming? No matter what is happening—whether you’re caught in your emotions, struggling with your thoughts, or dealing with life’s difficulties—something in you can always be looking higher. You don’t have to fight with what’s unfolding; you just need to keep even a small part of your attention on that higher place.

The mistake people make is thinking they have to deny what they are going through or force themselves to be something different. That’s not it. You live the life you have and go through what you need to go through, but you do it with an awareness of something greater. Keep your heart turned toward the highest, and that will change everything. When life pulls you into drama, you don’t have to get lost in it. You don’t need to judge yourself or others. You simply remind yourself—this isn’t all there is. There is something higher, and that’s where I’m going.

This path isn’t about struggle; it’s about surrender. If you let go, if you stop resisting, life itself will pull you forward. Everything you experience, every challenge, every difficulty, is there to help you grow. When you hold on to that truth, even pain and loss become part of the process of liberation. You don’t need to push away what’s happening—you just need to stop resisting. Keep your eyes on that higher place, and trust that what you’re going through will take you exactly where you need to be. That’s how you walk this path of surrender.

13-5.q: How can one maintain a spiritual focus without intense strain during purification periods?
13-5.a:
The first thing to understand about purification is that it’s a perfectly natural process. It happens when it’s meant to happen. Your job is not to control it, but to cease to resist it. Learn how to let go—not just during an intensive retreat or when doing a dedicated spiritual practice, but in the midst of your daily life. Every moment presents an opportunity to release something inside you that is holding you back.

A common mistake people make is thinking they have to go through a period of extreme spiritual focus—like three months of deep practice—and then return to their normal way of living. That’s not how real growth works. That’s like going on an extreme diet, losing weight, and then eating junk food again. Instead of separating spiritual work from daily life, integrate it into every single moment. Use your relationships, your work, your interactions— everything—as a means to let go of yourself and turn toward something higher.

You don’t need special time set aside to do this. There’s time within the time. While you’re working, while you’re in a conversation, while you’re feeling frustrated—there’s always a space within that moment to let go. You don’t have to wait for some designated spiritual practice to do the inner work. The world will bring up exactly what you need to let go of, and when it does, you simply release. That’s what purification really is—it’s life showing you what’s inside of you, and your job is to let it pass through without resisting.

It is true that sometimes things will come up intensely. You might feel fine one day and then suddenly be overwhelmed by emotion or resistance. That’s okay. That’s part of the process. If you make purification a natural part of your daily life, it won’t feel like some huge, overwhelming ordeal—it will simply be how you live. The middle way, the way of balance, is to use every experience as an opportunity to let go. When you do that, you’ll find that spiritual focus isn’t something you need to maintain with effort—it becomes the natural state of your being.

13-6.q: I’m doing a mantra more intensively, but it feels like the mental chatter fights back even harder. Should I keep pushing through it, or is there a better approach?
13-6.a:
When you do a mantra, it’s not about fighting with your thoughts. If you use it like a sledgehammer—trying to beat your thoughts down, trying to make them stop—you’re just creating more inner resistance. That’s the mind fighting with itself. When the mind fights with itself, there’s no real winner. You don’t want to use the mantra as a tool of suppression or control. That will only make the mental chatter push back even harder, just as you’re experiencing.

Instead, let mantra be a means to make a shift in your consciousness. When you use mantra, you’re not trying to get rid of thoughts; you’re simply choosing to place your awareness somewhere else. Your mind has layers— you know that. You can be doing one thing while thinking about another. Doing mantra is a way to shift into a higher layer of mind, where you’re not entangled with every little thought that arises. Just quietly say the mantra and lean back into it. Don’t worry if the thoughts are still there; they can come and go. Your job is not to fight them—your job is to rest your awareness in something higher, something lighter.

Over time, your consciousness will start to prefer that higher space. Just like when a song gets stuck in your head, it keeps pulling you back to it. The mantra should be like that—soft, gentle, something your awareness can naturally settle into. You’re not forcing anything. You’re not suppressing anything. You’re just letting go. Letting go is always about relaxing, not struggling. Yoga, true spiritual practice, is never about force. It’s like judo—you flow with the energy; you don’t resist it.

Your personal mind is simply the result of all the stored impressions and blockages from your past. That’s why it chatters, why it complains, why it stirs up so much noise. It’s just trying to release all that stored energy. Instead of fighting it, try something different—just love it. Like a child who’s upset, give it a little compassion. Say, “Hey mind, I hear you. I see you. You’re just expressing all the stuff I stored inside. That’s okay.” Give it a kiss on the forehead, so to speak, and let it be. Then return to your mantra. Not as a weapon, but as a gentle place to rest. You’ll see—if you relax into it, the mantra will take care of everything.

13-7.q: What are your teachings on noticing and embracing thoughts with loving kindness instead of resisting them?
13-7.a:
Noticing your thoughts without resisting them is a beautiful practice. Your mind is going to do what it does—thoughts will arise, patterns will play out, and emotions will surface. The question is, what is your relationship with all of that? Most people try to fight with their mind, pushing thoughts away and resisting what arises. But the mind isn’t something you need to control—it’s something you need to let go of. Instead of fighting with your thoughts, just let them be. Watch them with the same loving kindness you would give to a small child who doesn’t know any better.

When you see a thought arise, don’t judge it, don’t resist it, and don’t feed it. Just watch it. Let it be there, and instead of getting caught up in it, place your awareness above it. You don’t have to push it away—just recognize that you are the one who sees it. If you can, take it even further. Look at your mind with a little smile and say, “Oh, there you go again.” If you can do this with loving kindness toward your mind, you’ll notice that the thought starts to lose its hold on you. This is a very powerful method of letting go.

You can also offer those thoughts up. Instead of holding on to them, hand them over—to God, to the Universe, to something higher than yourself. Let them be taken from you. Every time a thought arises that pulls on you, you have a choice: Do you hold on to it, or do you let it go? The moment you choose to let go, you set yourself free.

The most important thing is that you’re using your will to rise above the mind, not to reinforce it. The problem isn’t the thoughts—it’s that you’re getting involved with them. Don’t fight or resist them. Just relax, watch, and let go. If you love your thoughts instead of fearing them, they will lose their grip on you. One day, you’ll find that you’re no longer stuck inside of them— you’re resting in the freedom of your own awareness.

13-8.q: I am struggling with some overwhelming emotions after a breakup. I am not sure if I am relaxing and releasing correctly because my emotions are so intense. How do I maintain clarity while allowing these energies to move through me?
13-8.a:
Thank you for sharing. You can be sure you are not alone in experiencing strong emotions after a breakup. Everyone on the path goes through such overwhelming energies at one time or another. There are two different approaches to dealing with overwhelming energy when it comes up. The first is to try to rise above the energy, using techniques that leave you centered in the face of the release. Meditation, mantra, positive thinking, yoga asanas, and other such practices are all techniques for maintaining your center when being pulled into the disturbed energies.

When this is not even close to working, there is another technique you can try. It is not about staying above the disturbance; it is solely about letting it pass through you. For example, when the emotional pain is overwhelming and you can’t stay above it, lie down on the floor on your back with your arms out to your sides. Relax your whole body, then raise your chest up toward the ceiling, and offer the energies you’re feeling to God, the Divine Mother. Let her take it all from you. You don’t have to deal with it; give it to her. She knows how—you don’t. Raising your chest up is inviting her to reach her hand in and take it all out. Keep relaxing the area around your heart. Let the disturbed energy release. Love the release, love the pain—it’s the pain that ends all pain. It has come to liberate you from yourself. Welcome the process of purification. Childbirth has pain; so does soulbirth. You are not doing anything—you are letting it happen. This is very deep spiritual growth.

13-9.q: How can I handle profound spiritual experiences without becoming ungrounded?
13-9.a:
If you have profound spiritual experiences, don’t hold on to them as part of your identity. No matter what you experience—no matter how high, how deep, how expansive—don’t let your mind get involved in defining yourself by it. The moment you start thinking, I had this experience, I must be special, I must be enlightened, you’ve lost the very thing the experience was offering you: freedom from your ego. The ego will always try to co-opt positive experiences and make them about you, but that’s not the spiritual path. The path is about becoming nobody, not somebody.

The experience itself is not the problem. Spiritual experiences can be beautiful, profound, even life-changing. What matters is what you do with them. If you let the experience shape your self-concept, it will create a separation between yourself and life. You will start living in your mind’s idea of spirituality rather than in the reality of the present moment. That’s how people get lost. They become disconnected from life, from others, from the very flow of the universe they were trying to merge with.

Instead, take the experience as grace. It’s not yours—it was given to you. You didn’t create it, you didn’t earn it, and you certainly didn’t make the universe reveal it to you. Just bow your head and say, “Thank you.” That’s it. Then go sweep the floor. That’s what keeps you grounded. You don’t chase the experience, you don’t define yourself by it, and you certainly don’t let it create distance between you and the simple, ordinary beauty of everyday life.

The real measure of spirituality is not how high you go in a momentary experience, but how balanced and present you are in daily life. If you can’t stay open and at peace on this plane, what makes you think you can handle higher planes? If an experience leaves you ungrounded, it wasn’t the experience itself but how you related to it. You let the “I” touch it. That’s the danger.

So let go. Stay humble. Recognize that the personal self is nothing. When you truly let go of it, something far greater than you can flow through you. That is where real spirituality begins—not in defining yourself as someone who had an experience, but in becoming nobody so that Truth itself can move through you, untouched.

13-10.q: What is the power of gratitude, and how does it affect perception?
13-10.a:
If you want to understand the power of gratitude, you have to stop looking for something specific to be grateful for. Gratitude isn’t about picking and choosing—it’s about seeing reality as it is and realizing it’s all a gift. Just look at what’s in front of you right now. Look at the sky, the trees, the people, the fact that you can hear, see, and breathe. Every single moment of existence is an absolute miracle. If you could step back and actually see what’s happening—the way trillions of cells work together to form a human body; the way a seed knows how to grow into a plant; the way the entire universe has managed to exist for billions of years—you wouldn’t need to manufacture gratitude. You would live in it.

The problem is, you let your mind get in the way. It decides what it likes and doesn’t like, what it wants and doesn’t want. If you dropped all that, you wouldn’t need to change anything to feel gratitude. You’d just prefer whatever is happening. The sun is shining—beautiful. It’s raining—amazing. Life is giving you something pleasant—thank you. Life is challenging you—I love it. Because all of it is miraculously unfolding by itself, all of it is an opportunity to grow.

This isn’t some philosophical game—it’s the highest form of living. When you are truly grateful, you are in harmony with life itself. Gratitude isn’t intellectual; it’s not about comparing what you have to what others have or trying to convince yourself to appreciate something. It’s about waking up to the fact that right here, right now, you are witnessing the unfolding of something far greater than yourself. Instead of fighting with life, you surrender in awe.

You might think you need a reason to be grateful, but the truth is gratitude is the natural state of a clear mind. The only reason you don’t feel it all the time is because your mind gets caught up in preferences, judgments, and personal narratives. The deeper you let go, the more you’ll see that every single moment is a gift. When you live that way, life becomes effortless. Gratitude isn’t something you practice—it’s something you become.

14-1.q: Can we learn everything we need from books, or do we need a spiritual teacher?
14-1.a:
The answer is that life itself is your teacher. You don’t have to go looking for a guru, because every single moment of your life is teaching you exactly what you need to learn. The real question is: Are you paying attention? Are you willing to let go and surrender to what life is showing you? Because that’s where the real growth happens.

Books can help. Teachers can help. They can point you in the right direction, offer clarity, and help you see things you might not have seen on your own. But in the end, the work is yours. You have to deal with your life. You have to be able to handle your relationships, your job, and your responsibilities. You have to learn to be okay regardless of whether you have money or not and whether things go your way or not. If you don’t, then all the books and teachers in the world won’t do you any good—because you can still be disturbed by what life throws at you. If you’re still clinging to your personal self and trying to make life be the way you think it should be, then you’re missing the whole point of spiritual growth.

Spiritually, the most important thing is your motive. What do you really want? If your motive is pure—if you genuinely want to let go of yourself, to be free, to grow—then everything will align for you. Life will bring you exactly what you need, whether it’s a book, a teacher, a difficult situation, or a moment of insight. It will all serve your journey. And yes, looking back, you may see that you didn’t always get it right, that you made mistakes—but that’s part of it. You have the right to grow, to change, to evolve.

But if your motive is to build up your ego, to use spirituality to make yourself feel more special, then that’s exactly where you’ll end up—trapped in yourself. You end up where your motive is. It’s not about what happens outside; it’s about what’s happening inside. The heart of the path is in your willingness to surrender, to let go and trust life.

So, don’t worry about whether you need a teacher or a book. Worry about your motive. If you’re sincere, life will take care of the rest. Everything you need will come to you at exactly the right time. Just stay open, stay honest, and let go.

14-2.q: How do I find a guru or spiritual teacher?
14-2.a:
When you ask about finding a spiritual teacher, what you’re really asking is: How do I find guidance on this path? How do I make sure I’m moving in the right direction? The truth is, when you’re truly ready, the teacher appears. That’s how it works. Not because you went out and found them, but because your sincerity opened the door for them to come into your life—whether as a person, a book, an experience, or even an inner knowing.

You don’t need to go searching. Every master that has ever walked the face of the earth—living or passed—will help you if you are truly open. The grace and guidance you are looking for is always there. A great master once said that grace is everywhere, pouring down like rain. But we hold up the umbrella of ego, making sure we don’t get wet. We protect ourselves from the very thing we’re asking for. The question isn’t, Where do I find grace? The question is, Am I willing to put down the umbrella?

The Real Spiritual Teacher 	129

Your real work is not going out to find a guru—it’s letting go of yourself. Let go of the mental noise that says the answers are always outside you and that you need to find them. The moment you stop clinging to that, you’ll see that life itself is grace. Everything you need is already coming to you. But if you insist on holding on to your fears and doubts, and your constant need for more than what life is already giving you, you’ll miss it. Let go, trust, be open, and you will know everything you need to know.

14-3.q: Do the teachings of Christ relate to yoga, and if so, how?
14-3.a:
Yes, Christ’s teachings absolutely relate to yoga—because yoga, in its highest sense, is about union. It’s about letting go of the personal self and merging with something much greater. That’s what Christ was pointing to. When he said to turn the other cheek, he wasn’t just talking about an external action. He was talking about what happens inside of you. Life is going to come at you—it always does. People will say things; situations will challenge you; difficulties will arise. What did Christ say to do? Let go; don’t resist; stay open. That’s what it means to turn the other cheek. You turn away from resistance and allow life to pass through you without disturbance. That’s inner freedom.

Look at what else he said. He told you that as he sits in the presence of the Father, you are meant to sit there too. He didn’t say, “I’m up here and you’re down there.” No, he basically said, “You will do even greater things than I have done.” That’s an extraordinary statement. What does it mean? It means that the state he reached is available to you, to everyone. That’s the highest yoga. It’s not about bending your body into poses; it’s about transcending the personal self—rising above that little mind that gets caught up in fear, judgment, and resistance. It’s about merging with something much greater, stepping into a state of pure openness, pure presence, just like he did. Christ called it dying to be reborn.

When you honor Christ, or Buddha, or any great being, you’re not worshiping a person. You’re honoring the state they reached, the state they encouraged you to reach. That’s a very beautiful thing. It’s an inspiration, a reminder of what’s possible. That’s why as you grow and you deepen your understanding of yourself, you will deepen your respect for Christ and the great masters. They weren’t just teaching rules or morality; they were teaching the highest truth—the path to absolute liberation.

14-4.q: How can I spread the truth about higher consciousness to people who are resistant or rooted in traditional beliefs?
14-4.a:
If you want to help people wake up, don’t focus on changing them—focus on bringing the highest version of yourself into every moment. That’s how you truly spread truth. You don’t have to argue with people’s beliefs. Just be the presence of truth, be the embodiment of openness, peace, and clarity, and that alone will have an effect far beyond what you can imagine.

People are at different levels of receptivity, and you can’t control when or how someone will be ready to hear something deeper. You may say something, and it seems like it goes nowhere, but years later, when their life shifts, they remember. That’s how truth works—it plants a seed. Sometimes that seed sits dormant for years, and then one day, when the right conditions arise, it blossoms. It’s not your job to force that timing; it’s your job to share truth as purely and openly as you can, then let go.

If you try to push against people’s beliefs, you’ll meet resistance. If you simply live in truth, embodying a higher way of being, people will feel it. They may not even realize what’s happening, but something inside them will shift. When the time is right, they will remember that feeling. That’s how transformation happens—not through force, but through the quiet power of presence.

Don’t worry about changing anyone. Don’t worry about who agrees with you or who doesn’t seem interested. Just keep growing, keep expanding, keep deepening your own connection to truth. When you do that, people around you will shift naturally, because truth is contagious. You don’t have to convince anyone of anything—just be the light, and the rest will take care of itself.

The Real Spiritual Teacher 	131

14-5.q: How can I support my partner without becoming frustrated when they don’t adopt the same teachings I follow?
14-5.a:
If you truly want to support your partner without frustration, stop trying to be their teacher. It is not your job to fix them, change them, or get them to follow the same teachings you do.
