If you stay open in this way, something very powerful will happen. Either the other person will be affected by the depth of your love, and they will open as well, or they won’t. If they don’t, they will naturally fall away. You don’t have to force anything. Let life decide who stays and who goes. Your only job is to keep honoring the love that is within you, to let it flow, and to never let anything or anyone take it away from you.

19-5.q: I’m in a happy, committed relationship, but a past relationship keeps popping up in my heart and mind. I don’t understand what is going on, and I don’t like it. Can you suggest guidance to free me from this?
19-5.a:
Thank you for your beautiful, deep question about the ways of the heart. All I can share is what a committed spiritual seeker would try to do in that situation.

1.	Do not ever feel guilty about love in the heart. It is beautiful that the heart feels love—that is what it is supposed to do.

2.	The key is to honor the flow of love through the heart, but gently work on redirecting it. You can channel the love toward your partner, your children, your work, God, or any other positive force that aligns with your commitments in life.

3.	Someone once asked a great yoga master if there is any technique that guarantees enlightenment in this lifetime. He said yes—put your attention at the point between your eyebrows and never take it off. That is a technique for rechanneling all your personal energies towards a higher center of consciousness (the sixth chakra). You have been struggling to redirect the energy flow passing through the fourth chakra—the heart chakra. Bring it up higher; breathe it up to the point between your eyebrows. Never push it back down—always raise it up. You have decided not to express yourself in ways that would interfere with your life’s commitments, and that’s beautiful. You are very powerful in there, and you have the ability to redirect the energy upward. It takes time, but it is always worth it to align your energy flow with your life’s aspirations.

4.	That is the answer in a nutshell. Do not feel ashamed or guilty for the energy flow through the heart. Rejoice that love exists in your heart. Now gently offer the love up to God. Raise the energy to the highest place you can imagine. The way the energy is flowing now is just a habitual flow the heart got used to. It’s not bad; it’s just misguided for this time and place. It will not take you where you have chosen to go. But you can, over time, rechannel that energy flow. Work with it. Turn the flow into something that supports the meaning of your life. Just keep raising it up, and you will become greater at everything you do.

19-6.q: Why do I feel like I close myself off because I care too much? If I practice spiritual detachment, isn’t that really a lack of caring?
19-6.a:
When you feel the need to protect yourself from caring too much, take a deeper look to see what is really happening. When something happens to someone you love, it creates discomfort inside of you. Maybe they are suffering, and that suffering bothers you. Maybe they are struggling, and that struggle makes you uncomfortable. Rather than learning to sit with that discomfort, you close. But closing isn’t a result of caring—closing is a reaction to your own inability to handle what’s happening inside of you.

Real caring isn’t about being disturbed when someone else is struggling. That doesn’t help them, and it doesn’t help you. If you are suffering because someone you love is suffering, now there are two people suffering instead of one. What if you could be the one who stays open? What if you could be the one who brings love, strength, and peace into the situation? That’s what true caring is. It’s not about taking on someone else’s pain—it’s about being fully present with them, while still remaining centered in love.

Detachment is not a lack of caring. It’s the highest form of caring. It means you can be there, fully open, fully available, without being pulled into the turbulence of the situation. You don’t resist what’s happening; you simply let it move through you, honoring it, accepting it, and bringing love into the moment. That is compassion, and that is what allows you to serve others without losing yourself in their struggles.

Don’t confuse closing with caring. You don’t need to close and protect yourself. You need to remain open so you can be a presence of love and support no matter what is happening. If you do that, you’ll see—there’s no need to shut down. You’ll be able to stay open to life as it unfolds and bring your deepest presence to every moment.

19-7.q: How do I stop judging others and embrace compassion in daily life?
19-7.a:
To stop judging others, the first thing you need to understand is why you judge in the first place. Judgment comes from the ego—plain and simple. The ego creates a self-concept, an idea of who you are, and then it spends its entire life reinforcing that idea. I do this, I don’t do that. I’m this kind of person, not that kind of person. Because the ego needs to be right, it judges everything that doesn’t fit into its little framework. How could they act like that? Why don’t they take care of themselves? Why don’t they see things the way I do? That’s all ego. It’s your mind trying to convince you that you’re right and the way you live is the correct way. That’s why judgment feels so automatic—it’s just the ego protecting itself.

The real shift happens when you start to see what’s actually going on inside you. If you can notice yourself judging, that means you—the real you—are already separate from the act. You are the one watching the judgment happen. That’s growth. That’s awareness. Most people don’t even recognize that they’re judging because they’re completely identified with their thoughts. Once you can objectively see judging happening, don’t try to force it to stop; just watch it. Let it be there. The more you observe it without getting caught in it, the more it will fall away naturally.

As the act of judging starts to drop, something else will take its place— compassion. When you stop filtering the world through the lens of your ego, you begin to see people for who they really are. That person who doesn’t take care of themselves, who struggles in ways you don’t understand—what must it be like inside them? What must it feel like to wake up in their reality, inside their mind, with their past? You think it’s hard dealing with your own thoughts? Imagine living inside theirs. When you start seeing others that way, judgment disappears on its own. It’s no longer, How could they be like that? but My God, how must it feel to be in there? That’s where true compassion comes from.

Remember, you cannot force yourself to feel compassion. All you can do is keep letting go of yourself—the part of you that needs the world to fit into your made-up framework. Judgment is not the core problem; it’s just a symptom. The real work is stepping back and releasing the grip your ego has on you. When you do that, judgment falls away naturally, and compassion takes its place—not because you forced it to, but because it was always there, waiting for you to move out of the way.

19-8.q: What is the significance of forgiving myself, and how does it impact my relationships with others?
19-8.a:
If you truly forgive yourself for the mistakes you made in the past, it changes everything. You don’t just stop judging yourself—you free yourself. When that happens, something profound takes place: you naturally begin to forgive others. Once you see that you don’t have to carry the weight of your own past mistakes, you realize no one else has to either. You stop judging them and holding on to past resentments. Forgiveness isn’t something you do—it’s something you become.

The moment you start practicing self-forgiveness, you see how easy it really is. The only thing that ever made it seem difficult was your resistance to letting go. You realize you don’t need to hold on to all these old judgments about yourself. You made mistakes—of course you did. You were five years old, or you were a teenager, but you were doing the best you could with what you knew at the time. Why would you keep punishing yourself for that? When you let it go, the relief is immediate.

So, the effect that forgiving yourself has on your relationships is simple: it heals them. The more you let go of yourself, the more space you create for others. You stop trying to control everything; you just experience people as they are. That’s real forgiveness. That’s real freedom. When you do this, you’ll find something incredible—you’ll look around, and suddenly, everyone in the world feels like your friend.

19-9.q: How can I have compassion for those who commit terrible acts?
19-9.a:
To have compassion for those who commit terrible acts, you have to start with reality. The reality is that these things happen. People harm each other; there are wars; there is suffering; and there are actions you may find unthinkable. Closing your eyes to reality or resisting it internally doesn’t change anything; it only disturbs you further. If you are hating what is, you are just fighting reality, and reality always wins. Accepting reality does not mean condoning these acts, but it does mean starting from a place of clarity instead of resistance.

Once you have accepted that these things happen, you can begin to ask a deeper question: Why do people do these things? You may not understand it because you haven’t lived their lives. You didn’t grow up in their circumstances; you didn’t go through the same suffering, conditioning, or trauma that shaped them. That doesn’t mean you justify their actions, but it does mean you recognize that every person is the result of countless influences you will never fully comprehend. If you had lived exactly their life, who’s to say you wouldn’t have ended up doing the same things? As the proverb says: “There, but for the grace of God, go I.”

This understanding brings forth compassion. Compassion is not about excusing behavior—it’s about not letting your heart close. If you let yourself be consumed with judgment, hate, and anger toward those who do terrible things, you have brought that darkness into yourself. What good does that do? What good does your internal suffering do for the world? If anything, you are just adding to the very energy that caused these things in the first place. Instead, step back, take a breath, and create space for a deeper truth— one that both recognizes the pain caused by the terrible act and understands that every being is shaped by their journey.

Dare to be the person who does not shut down, who does not add more division, but instead holds space for understanding. You are here to rise above the darkness that created the suffering, not to fall into it yourself. The more you let go of your resistance, the higher you will rise. From that higher place, real change can take place.

20-1.q: What does it mean to transmute energy, and how can I achieve this?
20-1.a:
If you want to understand how to transmute energy, you have to start by seeing how energy moves inside of you. When something happens that stirs up an inner reaction, you feel a pull—an intense, almost magnetic force that tries to drag your awareness down into the disturbance. The first step is to recognize that pull. Just notice it. You don’t have to fight it or push it away. And you don’t have to let it take you under. Simply witness it. That alone is a profound shift, because now you are separate from it. You are not the energy itself—you are the one experiencing it.

Now, instead of collapsing into the experience, you do something radical: you stay centered and allow the energy to rise. This is transmutation. You are not suppressing anything, nor are you indulging in it. You are creating the space for the energy to pass through you, without clinging to it or resisting it. Instead of going down into the old habitual patterns of reaction, you let the energy come up to you. You welcome it, like a wave rolling through, and you watch it release into a higher state.

If you want to see this clearly, think of a rope being pulled taut. At one end of the rope is your samskara—your stored past impressions—trying to pull you down into it. The other end is you, holding on to the rope, struggling not to get pulled in. Letting go isn’t about being strong enough to win the battle; it’s simply about opening your hands. The moment you release the rope, the tension disappears, and you are free to continue your journey upward. That’s how transmutation happens—not through effort, but through surrender.

20-2.q: Does yoga transcend physiology as well as psychology? For example, can stored emotions in the body be released through yoga?
20-2.a:
When energy gets blocked, it doesn’t just stay in your mind or heart—it manifests in your body. That’s why you might feel tension in your shoulders, tightness in your chest, or knots in your stomach. It’s why emotions seem to settle into different parts of your body, like trauma in your hips or stress in your neck. This is real, and it’s why practices like acupuncture, massage, and various body-based therapies can bring relief. They help move the energy, clear the pathways, and allow blockages to release.

But here’s what you need to understand: If you only work on the body, you’re not getting to the root of the problem. The reason the energy is stuck in the first place is because the mind and heart are holding on to things. The more you hold on to the fears generated by deep-seated patterns from the past, the more the energy has no choice but to lodge itself somewhere. That’s why, even after a massage or a therapy session, the tension often comes right back. You’ve only treated the symptom, not the cause.

The real work happens inside. The more you let go of resistance within your mind and heart, the more these blockages naturally dissolve. That’s why practices like yoga, meditation, and deep inner surrender are so powerful. When you stop inwardly resisting life, the body doesn’t need to store those blocked patterns anymore. The energy that was stuck can begin to flow again.

So yes, work with yoga or body-based therapies if they help you release, but don’t rely on them alone. The deeper healing comes when you learn to let



life pass through you without resistance. That’s where true freedom is—when nothing inside of you is stuck anymore.

20-3.q: Why is my body holding tension despite mentally surrendering, and how do I let that go?
20-3.a:
The physical body gets the energy—the shakti—after it passes through the mental and emotional bodies. Even the slightest disturbance in the energy flow coming into the physical body can cause imbalance. That is why people get ulcers from worrying, and so on. Here are some suggestions that may help as you continue to cleanse your mental and emotional systems:

1.	First, it is important to understand that while you are letting go of mental and emotional disturbance, some of the disturbed energy can still make it into the physical body. Be sure to relax the physical body while you are working with the energy. Relax your shoulders, relax your chest around your heart area, relax your tummy, and relax your buttocks. Breathe while you are relaxing. On the exhale, blow out any tension that has been released.

2.	Treat the body as though it were a little child getting scared by the disturbed energy coming into it. When you get a chance, give it a hug and speak nicely to it. Your physical body is an animal, and animals get very scared at the slightest thing. They can either tighten up and attack to protect themselves, or run away. Your body has inherited these tendencies of fight or flight. However, you are more evolved than your body, so reach down periodically and encourage it to relax. Tell it things are fine, and it doesn’t have to protect itself from the disturbed energy that leaked through. Just relax, relax, relax, and let go of any reactive tightening.

3.	Keep working with yourself in this way, and over time your body will stop reacting to uncomfortable energy. It can learn to be okay with disturbances.

20-4.q: Why do samskaras keep returning even after I try to release them?
20-4.a:
When deep samskaras come up again and again, it’s not because you’re doing something wrong; it’s because you’re only releasing some of their energy, not the root samskara itself. Every time a past experience or trauma resurfaces, what’s actually happening is a piece of its stored energy is coming up into your awareness. When you consciously relax and release that energy instead of resisting it, you’re doing exactly what you need to be doing. But that doesn’t mean the whole samskara is gone—it just means another layer has been lifted.

The mistake would be to think that because the thought or emotion came back, you’re not truly letting go. That’s not the case. You’re doing the work. You’re simply meeting these blocks at the level they’re ready to be released at the time. Releasing samskaras is not an overnight process—it’s a process of patience, openness, and trust. The best thing you can do is to stop resisting what’s coming up. When something arises, instead of thinking, Oh no, not this again, try saying, “Great—another chance to let go.” The more you welcome it, the easier the process becomes.

It’s also important to recognize that your mind will want to judge the process. It will want to say, “Why is this taking so long?” or “Am I doing something wrong?” None of that helps. The only thing that helps is learning to embrace each moment of release as it comes. Let whatever is surfacing be there. Don’t push it back down. Just relax and allow the energy to pass through you. That’s all you can do, and that’s all you need to do.

At the deepest level, this is about opening. The more you let go, the more you open. As you open, more will rise up to be released. That’s a gift. That’s life working to free you. The process is already happening—your only job is to stop interfering with it. Always welcome it, embrace it, and let it take you into a world of more and more love and freedom.

20-5.q: I’ve been letting go of my blockages on a daily basis, and it’s working. But I feel more neutral than joyful. When will I begin experiencing constant joy?
20-5.a:
It is very good that you are not being bothered as much by your daily life. That is a very good start to your spiritual growth. It is what we call “non-negative,” but it is not yet positive. You are using your will to avoid the negative energies when they come up, and that is certainly better than getting caught in them. But the shakti that has been blocked down there for years is still not totally free to flow upward. We have all developed personalities that keep our blockages at bay. We are in there holding it all together on a moment-to-moment basis. If we don’t change this at the root, the best we can get is neutrality.

Witness consciousness is the state in which you are noticing that you are holding it all together. Notice your mind’s thoughts; notice how your heart processes emotions. If you do this, you will see an underlying protectiveness going on at a very deep level. That is what you surrender and relax through—not just the moments when life hits your blockages. See if you can witness this deeper part of your being. And when you can see what is going on underneath, just relax and let go.

Remember, spirituality is not about letting go of life—it is about letting go of the parts of you that are protecting you from life. Once you see this, you’re doing great. Now, start working at an even deeper level. It will not be easy, but it is very much worth it.

The key is to remember that letting go is not a one-time event. It’s a practice. You may feel the pull again and again, but every time you make the choice to relax and let the energy pass through, you are working to rewire your entire way of being. Over time, the same energy that used to disturb you will become the very energy that lifts you. Once that upward flow begins, the joy for life becomes a reality. That is the beauty of this path—you are not trying to control the shakti; you are learning to set her free.

20-6.q: How can one feel passion in everyday tasks?
20-6.a:
When you talk about passion, you’re describing something very real. It exists in those moments when you become completely absorbed in what you’re doing, when there’s no separation between you and the task in front of you. It’s a merger, a oneness between consciousness and the object of consciousness. That’s a beautiful thing. True passion happens naturally when you are fully present, when you are so open that you become one with the moment itself.

Here’s the problem: most people can only experience that state when things are exactly the way the ego wants them to be. When you’re painting, playing music, or doing something you’re passionate about, you disappear into it. But the moment something happens you don’t like, you’re no longer in that flow. The ego blocks it.

The real question isn’t how to find things you are passionate about—it’s why you’re not passionate about everything. Taking out the garbage, washing dishes, or driving your kids to soccer is just as beautiful a task as anything else. The truth is, all of life is beautiful. It’s just that the mind has made distinctions, labeling some things as meaningful and others as mundane. If you learn to stay open, you’ll see that every single moment has the potential to be full of inspiration.

So don’t try to manufacture passion for certain things. Just be willing to let go of the blockages you have stored inside that interfere with your natural energy flow. Passion, love, inspiration—these aren’t things to be sought after. They are the natural state of a being who has stopped closing. Let go of the barriers, and you’ll see that life itself is ecstasy.

20-7.q: How do I respect each moment as unique and special?
20-7.a:
The moment that is unfolding in front of you is yours. No one else has ever experienced it before, and no one ever will again. That makes it unique, doesn’t it? But the mind doesn’t see it that way. The mind compares, judges, and decides which moments are special and which are ordinary. That’s the problem. There is no such thing as an ordinary moment. Life is extraordinary, but you miss it because you’re too busy deciding how you want it to be.

How do you learn to respect each moment as unique and special? You stop making it about you—about what you want and what you don’t want. The moment is already whole, already perfect in its own way. Your job isn’t to manipulate it; it’s to serve it. And you serve the moment by being fully present for it, without resistance, without preferences.

When you do this, you’ll notice something amazing. Instead of chasing after special moments, you’ll realize that every moment is special. Whether you’re sitting in traffic or standing on top of a mountain, there’s no difference.

The moment itself is enough. You don’t need to add anything to it.

If you learn to live like this, you’ll find that life takes care of itself. You won’t have to struggle to make things meaningful because everything will already feel full. The key is to stop making it about you and start showing up for life exactly as it is. Serve what is in front of you. That’s how you honor each moment.

20-8.q: How can you practice letting go without feeling indifferent? How do I reconcile putting all my energy into life with the concept of spiritual detachment?
20-8.a:
Be assured that letting go of your personal self does not lead to a state of indifference to life. It is really quite the opposite. While we are lost in thoughts and feelings of our own personal past, we are not connected to the present moment, and we are missing the true experience of life. You will find that when you let go of your personal self, you will actually feel more connected to life.

When you let go and are truly open to an experience, you let it all the way in. It actually moves you to the depth of your being. It becomes one with you, and you become one with it. This merger of the experiencer and the experience is a very spiritual state, and it transcends the noisy mind. You don’t have to recall that experience for it to affect you from then on. It has become part of your being, not just part of your mental collection of thoughts. It is beyond the psyche, not limited to it. These deep experiences make you more whole. When a river is free to flow unimpeded into the ocean, the waters merge and are no longer separate—they become one ocean, which is more complete than it was before.

When you go deep enough inside, beyond your personal mental and emotional panorama, you will find the source of love, compassion, and beauty. Your emotions are simply the ripples created by these energies manifesting in the lake of your psyche. When you let go of what you are watching, you will realize that you are the source of everything below you. You are not your thoughts; you are aware of your thoughts. You are not your emotions; you are aware of your emotions. The seat of Self is not a cold, indifferent place. The nature of Self is love, ecstasy, and divinity. When you stop clinging to the personal psyche, you’ll find you are much more than merely the human you’re watching—you are pure consciousness, experiencing the expression of itself in the form of reality.

20-9.q: What happens after one realizes and learns to stay in the seat of Self? How should one deal with distractions and samskaras?
20-9.a:
Once you are established in the seat of Self, you don’t need to do anything— you’re already complete. What happens naturally, however, is that you are so filled with love and inspiration that these beautiful energies want to express themselves. It’s like when you fall in love with someone—you don’t have to wonder what to do next; you just naturally spend time together expressing that love. The same is true with the inner flow of divine love. It flows out into the world expressing itself with everything you do, every moment of your life.

Right now, your actions are driven by fears and desires, by trying to make things be the way you want. You assume that if you remove all these psychological needs, there will be no motivation left. That’s not true. What’s left is something much greater. When you are fully centered in the Self, you don’t stop interacting—you just stop interacting out of personal needs. You do what you do because it naturally flows from within you. You serve, you create, you engage with life, but not because you’re trying to get something. You do it because you are constantly inspired to express the beauty within.

You don’t have to seek this inner energy flow. Just stay centered and learn to allow life to flow through you. The inner shakti flow is already there—you just have to stop blocking it. When samskaras come up, don’t resist them; just relax and let them pass. The more you do this, the more you will feel the shakti flow. Eventually, you will see that you don’t have to decide to do anything. Life will become the beautiful dance of expression between the inner and outer energy flows.

21-1.q: If the voice of my mind is telling me to relax and release, isn’t that just another layer of thoughts I’m aware of?
21-1.a:
Thank you for your very deep question. Think of it as a stairway to heaven— not a single leap. Consciousness identifies with what it is conscious of. In its most lost state, it actually uses the term “I” to express the thoughts it is caught up in. I like this, I don’t like that. I hope I get what I want; I pray I don’t have to experience what I don’t want. On and on it goes—never stopping, always thinking about how to control the world to match its preferences.

A giant step back is witness consciousness. You are aware that all of this is going on in your mind, but you are no longer totally lost in it or committed to it. In essence, you are conscious of being conscious of what you are conscious of. This is not enlightenment, but it is consciousness unbound from its addiction to the mind’s thoughts.

As an analogy, let’s say you are completely lost in watching a TV show. You are not aware of anything else in the room except what is on the TV. That is equivalent to how we typically interact with our minds. We are completely absorbed and identified with the mental show. Now imagine a commercial comes on the TV that you have no interest in. Suddenly you are back on the couch, aware of your body and the rest of the room. You have extricated yourself from your addiction to the show, but you are still on the couch, aware that the TV is on. That is the equivalent of witness consciousness. You are no longer totally absorbed in the mind’s thoughts, but you are still looking at the mind from a detached state.

When you are completely done with the TV, you can get off the couch and experience the rest of your life. When you are done with the mind, you— the consciousness—are no longer distracted by the mind’s thoughts, and you are free to stop looking in that direction. Just as when you get off the couch there is a whole world for you to experience, so when you stop looking in the direction of your mind’s thoughts, you realize you are not finite—you are universal.

You must pass through the state of witness consciousness in order to become detached from your addiction to your thoughts. Once you can see a thought as just a thought, you are ready to let it go. Once you can see all thoughts as just thoughts, you will no longer be distracted by them. Consciousness, not distracted by objects of consciousness, has returned to its Source—this is enlightenment.

21-2.q: How can I separate my mind from consciousness?
21-2.a:
You don’t have to separate the mind from consciousness—they are already separate. The only reason it feels like they’re not is that you’re so used to focusing on your mind that you’ve lost sight of yourself as pure consciousness. Think of a light shining on an object. The light has nothing to do with the object—it’s just illuminating it. Your consciousness is the light, and your mind is the object. But because you’ve been staring at the mind for so long, you think they’re the same.

The key isn’t figuring out how to separate them; that’s just the mind thinking about itself. Instead, start by noticing that you are the one who is aware of the mind. Your thoughts come and go, but something in you remains constant—the awareness itself. If you were truly your thoughts, you wouldn’t be able to observe them. But you can. You can watch your mind talk, analyze, worry, and dream. If you can watch something, then you are not that thing—you are the one who is watching.

The real question isn’t how to separate yourself from the mind, but why you are so attracted to it in the first place. Why does every little thought, every little emotional disturbance, pull your awareness into it? That’s what you need to let go of. When the mind says, I feel lost or I need to figure this out, don’t grab on to that thought. Just relax. Let it go. The more you release, the clearer it becomes. You are not the thoughts, nor the emotions, nor the personal story playing in your head. You are the one who is aware of all of that.

If you keep letting go of what you are not, you will naturally settle into what you are. That’s the only way to truly know the Self. Don’t fight with the mind, don’t try to control it—just stop getting caught in it. Keep relaxing and letting go, and what you’ve been looking for will reveal itself. You’re already there—you just need to stop getting distracted.

21-3.q: What does it mean for consciousness to be distracted, and how can it return to its source?
21-3.a:
When you say that consciousness is distracted, you have to understand what that really means. Consciousness itself is always present, always aware, always whole. But it gets drawn down into thoughts, emotions, and external events. Consciousness is pure and untouched at its source. But as it projects outward, it appears to take on the characteristics of what it focuses on. If your awareness is completely fixated on a thought, a problem, or an emotion, it feels like you are those things. You are not. You are the one who is aware of them.

In truth, you don’t have to go anywhere to return to your seat of consciousness—you never really left. You’ve just been looking outward instead of resting in your true nature. Returning to your source actually means learning to not be pulled out of your source. It means recognizing that when something arises in the mind, you don’t have to follow it. You don’t have to leave your seat of consciousness to chase the thought. If you want to be free, you have to stop getting lost in the objects passing through.

The key is to let go. Let thoughts arise and let them pass. Let emotions come and let them go. Instead of being dragged down into them, simply observe them. That’s how you return home. That’s how you stay centered in the seat of consciousness. You don’t find your way back by struggling with the mind—you let go of the struggle entirely. You will then come to see that you were always there, but you were looking out instead of in.

21-4.q: Does shakti grow stronger as samskaras are released? What does it feel like to have no blockages?
21-4.a:
In the deep yogic teachings, one of the most beautiful names for God is Chit Shakti: Conscious Energy. When Einstein discovered that E=MC2, he scientifically unveiled a great mystery of the universe: there is no matter, just frozen energy. Just like steam, water, and ice are all just temporary states of the same substance, so the whole universe is just manifestations of the same underlying energy: shakti.

Your body, thoughts, and emotions are all shakti energy vibrating at different rates. The higher the vibration rate, the more beautiful the experience of the energy flow. Low, dark thoughts and emotions are heavy, while more elevated thoughts and emotions are light and uplifting. If you willfully resist an energy flow because you can’t handle it, it becomes a stored blockage, a samskara. The higher energy flows can’t make it past the lower blockages, just like water can’t flow freely through ice, even though they are the same substance. But when you work to release these blockages, it frees the shakti to vibrate at higher and higher levels, which is eventually experienced as bliss and ecstasy.

Note that this is just the shakti flow within the body, mind, and emotions. Since shakti energy is omnipresent, you are capable of experiencing your oneness with all. You just have to learn how to free your consciousness from its addiction to focusing on your tiny body, mind, and heart. That is what the teachings are gradually teaching you: how to let go of your false image of self. The more you let go, the more you will experience the shakti in her purer form. Eventually you will cease to experience yourself as separate from her—that is the state of the Great Merger. Christ said it this way: “I and my Father are one.”

21-5.q: Some teachers speak of super-consciousness. Is that really just another word for God?
21-5.a:
Consciousness identifies with what it is conscious of, especially when the object of consciousness is very distracting, like pain, the feeling of love, or a powerful experience that leaves a strong impression. We call that “the fall from the garden”—consciousness has totally lost itself in what it is aware of. Such is the human state.

When consciousness releases the tendency to identify with what it’s conscious of and remains in the seat of objective observation, we call that witness consciousness. In this state, consciousness is aware that it is experiencing the objects of consciousness, but it has not fallen down into or identified with those objects. It is simply aware, nothing more.

When consciousness is no longer distracted by what it is aware of, it naturally returns to the source of consciousness. This can be called the Great Merger, the return to oneness, the nondual state. When that merger into oneness is complete, that is the super-conscious state. All things are in you, and you are in all things. You have merged into the primal, unmanifest state before all was created. Your drop of consciousness has fallen into the ocean of consciousness—that drop exists no more—it has become the ocean.

21-6.q: What does it mean to live with awareness of your higher self while continuing to engage with your personality and everyday life? How does this affect the evolution of the soul?
21-6.a:
That’s a great question. First, understand that the terms “consciousness” and “soul” are just words pointing to something much deeper. If you try to grasp them with the mind, you’re going to get tangled up in concepts, instead of experiencing what they really mean. The truth is, you don’t have to define them—you have to experience them. But let’s at least use words to point in the right direction.

Consciousness is awareness itself. It’s that which notices everything— your thoughts, your emotions, the world around you. If I ask you to watch your thoughts right now, who is watching? That’s consciousness. It’s not personal; it’s not bound by your name, your history, or even your body. It is simply the presence of awareness, the part of you that has always been there, completely untouched by what it observes. Consciousness is not something you develop—it’s what you are.

The soul, on the other hand, is more of a personal expression of consciousness. You could think of it as an individual drop of the ocean of consciousness that moves through life, learning, growing, and evolving. It carries impressions, and even tendencies, from lifetime to lifetime. Your personality is that drop of consciousness identifying with what it is aware of—your body, thoughts, and emotions. Meanwhile, the ocean of pure consciousness remains untouched, transcendent, identifying itself as the ocean, not the drop.

The key is to not get caught up in definitions, but to shift your attention toward what is real. If you sit quietly and notice that you are aware of experiencing this moment, without getting lost in thoughts about it, you are touching pure consciousness. If you open your heart, if you align yourself with the highest within you, that’s the unfolding of the soul’s journey. The beauty is that as you go deeper, you’ll see that the two are not separate at all. The soul longs to merge back into the ocean of pure consciousness, to let go of its individual limitations and return to its true nature.

Don’t worry about defining it too much. Just watch. Just be. The more you let go, the more you’ll come to know—not with your mind, but with direct experience—what consciousness, soul, and personality really are.

21-7.q: You say that Earth is a place souls are sent to evolve. I thought the soul was perfect, complete—how does it evolve?
21-7.a:
The Self, or soul, is the perfection of God’s consciousness staring at your mind, your body, your emotions, and what comes in through your senses. Just as you can get lost in watching a TV show and completely forget you are a human sitting on the couch, so a ray of God’s consciousness gets so distracted by what it is staring at that it forgets who it really is. This is how God takes on the self-concept of a human being.

The evolution of the soul is not about perfecting God’s consciousness— it is already perfect. It is about freeing that ray of consciousness from its addiction to staring at what it is not. Spiritual enlightenment is like finally freeing yourself from being completely absorbed in the TV show and standing up to remember who you really are. That is why Yogananda called spiritual awakening self-realization.

21-8.q: Do you believe our consciousness transcends death? If so, do we retain our personality?
21-8.a:
Science says, “Energy is neither created nor destroyed.” Likewise, the great masters say, “Consciousness is neither created nor destroyed.” Consciousness is and always was aware—it’s just a question of what it’s aware of. Thus, at the death of the body, consciousness does not change; it just becomes aware of things other than what the body’s five senses pick up.

As far as your personality is concerned—your habitual thought and emotional patterns—it is not made of physical substance and does not fall apart at the body’s death. So, unfortunately, you take your mess with you! That is why it is so important to clean out your stored disturbances while you’re alive.

Ultimately, when a truly great being dies, they are free to fall all the way back into the source of consciousness because there are no past mental or emotional patterns binding them. That is what is meant by merging with God. We call this the ultimate liberation. At this point, you have truly died of the personal and are reborn in the spiritual. Life’s entire journey is the evolution of individual consciousness back to the state of Oneness.

The Meaning of Life and Death.name: The Meaning of Life and Death

22-1.q: What is the ultimate purpose of life?
22-1.a:
If you want to know the ultimate purpose of life, first look around. Everything you chase, everything you hold on to, everything you think matters so much—it all passes with time. It’s transient. You can build relationships, make money, raise a family, and there’s nothing wrong with any of that. But don’t mistake it for the meaning of your life. You are here for something much deeper.

You’re going to die soon—sooner than you realize. When that moment comes, none of what you’ve collected will go with you. The pharaohs tried to take it all with them, and they didn’t succeed very well, did they? But if everything external is temporal, then what is permanent? What is the real purpose of all this?

The purpose of your life is the evolution of your soul—your return to the divine. You are here to use every experience to lift yourself higher, to let go of what holds you back, and to merge into the greater flow of life. If you put your energy on your inner work, instead of clinging to life as it slips through your fingers, you will be investing in what is permanent, rather than what’s temporary.

So don’t get lost in the small stuff. Don’t think life is about arranging things the way you want. It’s about learning to let go, about realizing that each moment is an opportunity to free yourself. When you finally surrender, when you stop fighting and start flowing with life, you will see—you were never separate; you were never small. You were always part of something infinite. That realization is the purpose of your life.

22-2.q: You teach that I am just a tiny speck in the universe. I understand, but it’s overwhelming. How can I regain passion for life?
22-2.a:
When we take a universal perspective, it helps us avoid getting lost in the meaningless minutiae of our personal fears, desires, and reactions. Once you have that perspective, you can simply enjoy the natural unfolding of your life on this tiny planet. When your personal noise becomes meaningless, the miracle of life itself becomes meaningful. It becomes awe-inspiring that in the middle of vast, empty space, you are on a beautiful planet, experiencing a body, breathing air, feeling emotions, and thinking thoughts. You are conscious and honored to receive each breath and to engage with every experience that unfolds before you. This integrated experience of your life will create the connection you are seeking.

We all go through stages in our inner growth. If right now you are feeling disconnected and overwhelmed, experiment with just quietly receiving and appreciating the simple experiences in your environment. Notice the sensation of the earth beneath your feet, the air moving in and out of your lungs, the sensations you feel when you touch objects. Take a walk, wash some dishes, receive your life in a simple way, and let go of any fears of complexity. It is the mind that creates complexity and alienation.

Gently work on letting go of any anxieties that come up about being out of place. The very fact that you are alive and conscious means that you have a



very important place in life. Do you realize that nobody has ever experienced the exact moments you’ve experienced? If something exists and nothing is conscious of it, it has no meaning. But you are the consciousness that gave those moments meaning. Your place is to receive, experience, and love all the amazing parts of creation that pass before you. Consciousness is the most important thing in all of creation—and you are that consciousness.

22-3.q: I feel unfulfilled in my profession. I want to find something that I am truly passionate about. How do I discover my real purpose?
22-3.a:
Thank you for sharing the problem you’re having finding passion and purpose in your life. Passion and purpose are not something you find outside—they are something you have inside. When you start your car in the morning, you should be passionately excited that it started and that you get to drive to work. When you get to work, you can be passionately excited that you have a job, get to be of service, and actually get paid for doing it!

In essence, you are asking the wrong question about finding passion. The real question is what is blocking your natural passion for being alive and spinning on this tiny planet in the middle of vast, empty space. The great Persian poet, Rumi, once said, “Yesterday I was clever, so I tried to change the world. Today I am wise, so I am changing myself.”

Change how you’re looking at things, and your whole life will change. Work on being passionate about your current job, and if a new opportunity presents itself, wonderful—be passionate about that. You don’t have to look for a certain job or relationship in order to be passionate. You should be able to clear out the blockages that keep you from being excited about everything on this amazing planet. Or would you rather be on Mars, where nothing is ever happening?

If you want purpose, let this be your life’s purpose: Let go of the inner blockages that are stealing your shakti and keeping you from God. Be passionate about that purpose, and all of life will become a fantastic, passionate experience.

22-4.q: Are my life events part of a divine plan, or are they basically random?
22-4.a:
The purpose of your life is your soul’s evolution. But this does not unfold as we think it does. God is much more brilliant than we can comprehend. If two or more people are experiencing the same outer event, and each of them has separate evolutionary needs, how can the same nonrandom event be equally beneficial for the growth of each person?

To answer that perplexing question, you have to first understand that the event itself is not personal. It is simply the natural unfolding of the universe manifesting at that point of time and space—just like the quadrillions of other events happening at the same time. All of them are intricately tied together in a great perfection throughout time and space.

The reason the same event can be beneficial spiritually for each observer is because each observer is looking at the same event through “the eyes of the beholder.” They will experience the same event differently because of their own personal blockages from their past. In other words, the experience will stimulate different stored patterns in each observer, with their indwelling consciousness experiencing the event only after it has been tainted by these samskaras.

Thus, every event will be exactly what each individual needs to experience in order to stimulate the challenge of their inner growth. In essence, the universe is created with such perfection that it works perfectly for each individual. The event doesn’t have to be personal; you just have to take it as personal. That has exactly the effect needed in order to force you to deal with your blocked energies. When you are done with your personal blockages— that is, enlightened—you will see life as it really is: the manifestation of God.

22-5.q: Is the goal to always handle situations and then serve from that place?
22-5.a:
If you can’t handle a situation, you will be trying to manipulate it so you can handle it. When you do that, you’re serving yourself. You’re making life be about you—about what you need in order to feel okay. But if you can handle what’s happening, if you are fully okay inside no matter what unfolds, then something very different takes place. You no longer need to manage life for your own comfort, so you can turn your attention outward: How can I help? That’s the shift, and that’s where real service begins.

Look at life: If a person has fallen down, you help them up. Not because you’re trying to be a good person, but simply because that’s what is needed in that moment. If a butterfly is trapped in your car, you help it out. There’s nothing personal about it—it’s just the natural flow of serving what’s in front of you. That’s what a life of service looks like. It’s not about what you want or don’t want—it’s about what life is presenting you and how you can help.

The highest life you can live is one in which every moment that unfolds before you is better off because it interacted with you. That’s it. No big philosophy, no complicated concepts—just this simple truth: whatever moment comes to you, leave it better off than you found it. You don’t do this because you need something in return; you do it because you don’t need anything from the moment. When you are whole inside and don’t need life to fix or fulfill you, then all that’s left is to serve.

So yes, the goal is to serve. But don’t start with “How can I serve?” Start with “Can I handle this moment exactly as it is?” If the answer is no, then work on that. Work on letting go of the part of you that resists, that needs things to be a certain way. When you reach the place where nothing needs to be different, service happens naturally. It’s not something you do—it’s simply what flows from a being who is free.

22-6.q: You teach that each moment in life is experienced uniquely by each individual. What is the purpose of looking at life from this perspective?
22-6.a:
When you look at your life, you’ll see that every moment was experienced uniquely by you. No one else has ever had the exact sequence of moments you’ve had, and no one else ever will. In essence, you are God’s emissary sent to experience these moments of creation. If you’re not paying attention and miss the moment passing before you, no one will ever have experienced it. And even if you do experience it, you tend to resist it and judge it instead of appreciating it. You say, “I don’t want this moment; I want that one.” That’s the problem; you think you know which moments are supposed to happen. But the truth is, the moments unfolding are exactly what’s supposed to be happening—not in a moral sense, but based on the law of cause and effect. If you stop resisting them and start honoring them, life will become an incredible teacher for you.

Every moment you experience is a gift. It was made just for you. Think about that. Out of all the infinite possibilities, you are the only one who has ever had this exact moment in this exact way. The question is, will you respect it? Will you honor it? Will you see that life is shaping you, sculpting you like a great artist chiseling away at marble? Life isn’t here to build up your personal self—it’s here to break down the barriers that separate you from the truth. If you allow it to do its work—if you let go of your preferences and open yourself to what’s actually happening—you’ll begin to see the divine intelligence behind it all.

You struggle because you think life should be a certain way, that it should conform to your desires. The real path is to surrender to what is—to recognize that every moment serves your spiritual evolution. It’s all unfolding exactly as it should, and your job is not to fight it, but to embrace it. When you do that, gratitude naturally arises. You stop seeing life as a series of obstacles and start seeing it as a gift, as a direct expression of the divine calling you home. This is the power of surrender.

22-7.q: I am elderly and wish to continue finding purpose in my life. How do I move forward and be motivated to live fully and serve?
22-7.a:
We are so pleased that you are ready to move forward. Here is a beautiful daily prescription for life that will allow you to live fully and serve:

1.	When you wake up in the morning, remind yourself that the purpose of this day is to let go of whatever comes up that causes resistance in you. Commit to relaxing through events, thoughts, and emotions that are creating resistance. The overall purpose of your life, and death, is to go back up with less than you came down with. Now can you see you have a very important job to do with this day? Take that job seriously—it is the reason you took birth.

2.	Honor the moment unfolding before you, and see if there is anything you can do to uplift it as it passes by. Remember, no one

has ever seen that moment before, and no one ever will. It’s your moment. Treat it with respect, honor, and love. Give something to it as it passes by, even if that something is just a smile or the wink of an eye. Acknowledge how special you and the moment are to have shared this experience together. That includes not only people you come in contact with, but also the weather, the trees, the sun, and all of nature as it passes by. Just imagine if there was nothing in front of you, and learn to appreciate all the somethings that are there.

3.	When the day is done and it is time for sleep, sit up in bed and quietly look within. See if anything from the day has not yet passed through you. Realize it was just an event on a tiny planet spinning through vast, empty space. Let it go. Release it into the vastness of the billions of stars in your galaxy, of which your Sun is only one. The bothersome event only matters because you resisted it. Let it go; free yourself. There is great love, inspiration, and purpose inside of you. Let go of all these human frailties and soar up into your greatness. Do not hold this day’s pain inside you—or all that pain will be there in the future. Just honor its existence, give it a kiss on the head, and let it pass through you without resistance. This is not always easy, but it is what gives your life the purpose you seek. You have inner work to do— embrace it with great enthusiasm.

4.	Repeat this process daily.

22-8.q: Many people are very anxious about the topic of death. What happens to consciousness after death?
22-8.a:
The important question is not what happens to consciousness after death, but why do you even want to know? What is it in you that feels the need to conceptualize something you haven’t experienced yet? If you were entering a new relationship, would you really like to know what every interaction was going to be like? No, you’d want the joy of experiencing the moments for yourself, openly and fully. Death is the same way. You are going to find out what happens—you can be sure of that. You don’t need to clutter your mind with ideas that can’t possibly capture what you haven’t experienced. All you really need to know is that death is a once-in-a-lifetime experience, and when the time comes, you’ll see for yourself.

If you want to contemplate death, however, you first have to understand the nature of consciousness. Unlike your body, consciousness is not made of atoms. Right now, your consciousness is staring at the world through the lens of your body. But when the body is no longer there, consciousness won’t be staring at the physical world anymore. That doesn’t mean consciousness will cease to exist. Have you ever noticed how, even in dreams, you are still conscious? Your body is lying in bed, but your awareness is engaged in experiencing the dream. Likewise, when you get lost in thought, you don’t take your body with you. The mind, the personality, they’re not bound by physicality in the way we often assume. That at least gives you a clue as to what aspect of your being could remain after the death of the body.

What does that mean for you today? It means that if you’re carrying a heavy, negative mind when you leave this world, you might find yourself still entangled in it. If your mind is filled with unresolved fears, regrets, or attachments, and there’s nothing left to distract you from them, that could feel like hell. But if your mind is open, clear, and at peace—if you’ve done the inner work to let go of your past struggles—then what’s left? Just the beautiful, expansive openness of your true being. That’s why the great spiritual teachings emphasize letting go. And that’s why the masters have always encouraged raising your consciousness while you’re still here. Not because of some rigid doctrine or belief system, but because they understand that the state in which you live is the state in which you leave.

Don’t let the thought of death be something that weighs on you. Don’t let it be a source of fear. Instead, live in a way that when the time comes, you’re ready to go. Free yourself from the mental noise now. Then, when you get to that once-in-a-lifetime experience, you can step into it with grace, with peace, and with the openness to experience what’s next—whatever that may be. Trust me, you will find out.

22-9.q: How do you deal with grief when someone close to you passes away?
22-9.a:
When someone close to you passes away, grief is a natural experience. You formed a deep energetic connection with that person, and now it feels like that connection is gone. The energy inside of you, which used to flow freely through the heart, suddenly has nowhere to go. The heart closes down, attempting to protect itself, and the energy flow starts hitting those blockages, causing great pain and discomfort. Meanwhile, your entire self-concept becomes shattered because you can no longer define yourself based on your relation to that person. This causes a feeling of deep loss and confusion because, in a very real sense, you have lost the ability to relate to the world as you once did. That’s what grief is—the energy inside you reorganizing itself because it can no longer flow the way it used to.

What is the best way to deal with such a deep sense of loss? First, you have to accept it. Grief is not something to resist, deny, or judge. It’s not a psychological problem—it’s the natural result of a loss of connection. You don’t need to fight it or try to make it go away. The mind will want to get involved, telling stories, replaying moments, questioning what could have been different. That is just its way of releasing some of the blocked energy. In truth, it really doesn’t help that much. If you can stay present with the discomfort, allowing it to surface and move through you, that is the surest way to process grief without leaving long-term scars.

The key is to give grief space without sinking into it. That’s the mistake people often make—they either suppress grief, or they drown in it. You don’t need to do either. Instead, sit in the seat of awareness and allow the grief to come up to you; don’t go down to it. And have compassion for your heart. It’s going through a change—welcome the discomfort, while remaining clear and open to the experience.

Grief is part of the process of spiritual cleansing; don’t be afraid of it. If you need to, you can help rechannel the energy by breathing it upward. Focus on the center of your heart where the pain is, and take slow deep breaths inward and upward, releasing the energy into the vast universe with each breath. If you give the energy flow the space it needs, it will find its way to a higher place. Your heart will heal—not by closing, but by opening even more.

22-10.q: I recently lost my child to a serious illness. I’m feeling overwhelmed with grief. Are there spiritual practices that can help me release the pain of grief?
22-10.a:
We are very sorry to hear about your loss. It’s a beautiful question you’ve asked about how to release the pain while you grieve. The death of a loved one is difficult for anybody, and it takes time to heal.

This is how a spiritual person navigates the grieving process: they go through the human pain like any other person—except they do not resist the experience. If the heart hurts, they honor the heart’s right to feel those real feelings, and they just deeply relax and breathe through the heart. Breathe the pain upward, toward the point between your eyebrows—the spiritual eye. This creates a sense of openness and acceptance.

In the end, a spiritual person honors what their human heart is going through, while at the same time using the experience to explore the depths of their being. They do the same thing with the mind. The mind is going to try to cope with the pain by talking about what could or should have been. A centered person understands the mind and why it does what it does. They just relax behind it with a sense of compassion for the pain of humanness. Honor the mind’s right to cleanse, but don’t get lost in it. Behind it all is the peace of knowing that all things pass in time, if you let them, and you become greater for having gone through them consciously.

The key is to relax from a place deep inside. Honor what you are going through, but keep gently raising yourself. This is not just how an evolved spiritual person goes through difficulty—it is how one evolves spiritually.

23-1.q: What is intuition, and how can you distinguish it from mental projections?
23-1.a:
Intuition isn’t just another thought in your mind—it is your higher consciousness speaking directly through you. When you seek intuition from within your thoughts, you’re looking for it in all the wrong places. True intuition transcends the thinking mind entirely.

The moment you become concerned with distinguishing real intuition from mental projections, you’ve already introduced personal motive. You are seeking guidance for making the right decision or avoiding a mistake. But this very motive contaminates the purity of intuition. When your personal mind is attempting to use intuition to solve its personal problems, you can be sure it will be your personal mind you’re listening to. Genuine intuition does not come through coercion or mental striving—it simply unfolds naturally, without any inner effort.

The path to accessing true intuition is simple: remain present, stay open, and allow life to unfold naturally. When you release your attachment to controlling outcomes, you will remove the obstacles that block intuitive wisdom. You don’t need techniques to access intuition—you simply need to get out of the way. Let go of the personal self, with all its preferences and concerns, and truth will be effortlessly available. The deep wisdom of intuition emerges when your consciousness ceases to be bound to the ego-mind.

23-2.q: Does intuition require that I quiet my mind first?
23-2.a:
If you relentlessly practice relaxing and releasing the incessant mental chatter, things will become quieter inside. You will reach a state where you are just there noticing what is going on around you, both inside and out. Thoughts and feelings will arise in front of you, but they will not capture your attention enough to pull you into them. Yet without thinking, you will know things. You will just know that you know, to the core of your being. That is intuition.

If that intuition is inspiring you to manifest externally, very logical thoughts will arise to support that manifestation. Those thoughts have their root in the intuition, not in your personal psyche. You will eventually notice that the personal, psyche-driven thoughts bubble up from below where you sit inside, while the impersonal, intuition-driven thoughts come from above. This will eventually become as clear as day to you. The Surrender Experiment deals with the subtlety of this topic. You will get a lot from that book.

23-3.q: How can I differentiate between intuition and the mind’s interference?
23-3.a:
The first thing you need to understand is that intuition is quiet. It doesn’t argue with you, and it doesn’t try to convince you. The personal mind, on the other hand, is very loud. It talks and talks, trying to justify itself, trying to make sure you listen. It will even claim it is your intuition: “Trust your gut! You just know this is right!” But if it’s loud—if it’s filled with emotion, past experiences, fears, or desires—that is not intuition. That is your psyche. That is the voice inside your head, and that is what you need to let go of.

True intuition isn’t based on past experiences or personal fears. It’s not reminding you of how you got hurt before or warning you that something bad might happen again. That’s the mind trying to protect itself. Intuition is deeper than that. It doesn’t arise from personal likes and dislikes, from what you want or don’t want. It’s not tangled up in your conditioning. Instead, it’s a quiet knowing that simply is. It doesn’t have to convince you—it just arises naturally.

If you really want to touch intuition, first let go of all the noise. When a thought, a fear, or a strong desire comes up, relax and release it. If it’s not true intuition, it will pass. If it is real, it will still be there after you’ve let go of everything else. You don’t have to worry about missing something important—truth doesn’t disappear just because you relax. In fact, the only way to clearly perceive truth is by letting go of the personal noise that distorts it.

Life has a natural flow. If you stop trying to impose your personal preferences on reality, you will start to notice that things unfold in harmony. The outside world will align with what is deeper inside of you, and you won’t have to struggle to figure it out. That’s how you tell the difference between mind and intuition. If you’re caught up in thoughts and emotions, it’s the mind. If it’s quiet, clear, and unwavering, it’s intuition. Let go of the noise, and you will see.

23-4.q: I would like to know the role of prayer and surrender in situations involving serious illness, human suffering, and natural disasters. Does prayer really help?
23-4.a:
Yes, you are helping others when you pray. Your heart energy is like light; it travels vast distances and carries the heartfelt vibration of the sender. If you sincerely strive to let go of your personal preferences, fears, and desires that keep you bound to yourself, you will begin to feel God’s healing energy moving through you.

It is true that there is great suffering that goes on in this world. The willingness to recognize that fact and to keep your heart and mind open allows you to be a beacon of light in the darkness. If you get lost because you cannot handle the realities of life, you become part of the problem, not the solution. Heartfelt compassion is a very high form of prayer. The light that emanates from your heart when you are open is a truly powerful healing force.

23-5.q: Is prayer effective, and what is the highest form of prayer?
23-5.a:
Of course, prayer is effective. But you have to ask yourself: What am I praying for and why? If you are using prayer to ask for things—I want a car, I want people to like me—that’s a certain kind of prayer. That’s you trying to manipulate the universe to fit your personal preferences. The highest prayer is not about getting things for yourself; it’s about letting go of yourself. It’s about transcending your small, personal self and connecting with something much greater. The most meaningful prayers are for self-realization, for liberation, for removing the obstacles between you and God. “Not my will but thy will be done” is the highest prayer—it leads you beyond your personal wants and fears into something vast and infinite.

Praying for others is beautiful as well because it helps them and also moves your focus off your personal needs. The most transformative prayers are the ones that lift you beyond yourself altogether. You don’t have to pray for reality to be different. You can surrender to God’s will. You can say, Help me let go. Help me rise above this constant noise of my mind. When you pray like this, you open yourself up to something much greater than what your mind thinks it wants.

The most powerful prayer is not in words—it is in the action of letting go, again and again. It is allowing yourself to merge with the expansiveness of the universe—with God. As you do this, you will find that happiness and peace arise naturally because you stopped clinging to the small self that always wants something. You will become a beacon of light in this world, a channel for the light everyone is praying for.

23-6.q: What about prayer to attract to ourselves what we think we need? Or should prayer only be used to help others?
23-6.a:
When you pray for others, you’re engaging in something much higher than simply asking for what you personally want. When you ask for things for yourself—whether it’s material possessions, better circumstances, or even just comfort—you’re reinforcing the idea that you are not okay. You’re saying, I need this to be happy. That’s a form of taking. You’re trying to rearrange the world so it fits your preferences, so you can finally feel okay. If you look at it honestly, that’s a never-ending cycle. You get one thing, but then you need the next, and then the next. It keeps you trapped in a state of always needing something outside yourself.

Praying for others, for peace, for the well-being of the world—this is giving. It’s not about making the world fit your desires; it’s about offering something from within yourself. The less it has to do with your personal attachments—your family, your friends—the purer that giving becomes. When you sincerely say, May everyone be well, may everyone be free, may all beings find peace, you are moving beyond yourself. Little by little, this is the stairway to heaven. You are letting go of “me” and expanding into something greater.

Ultimately, as you grow spiritually, you begin to see that reality is not personal. The world is unfolding as it does because of the nature of things. Water is blue, flowers are red, and grass is green. When you stop resisting that, when you stop constantly trying to manipulate reality to fit your personal needs, something beautiful happens—you come into harmony with life. In that harmony, you become a blessing on the earth. You are no longer adding negativity, resistance, or struggle—you are adding peace.

Here’s the real secret—when you reach a certain state of inner peace, your very presence helps others. You don’t have to do anything. You contribute to the energy of the world in a meaningful way just by being. That’s why the great sages affect everything around them, simply by existing. It’s like the saying, “A high tide raises all ships.” A high being raises all people. In some traditions, monks and meditators dedicate their practice to uplifting all of humanity. It’s not just a belief; it’s a real effect. The deeper you go into your own peace, the more you naturally give that peace to the world.

So, yes, pray, meditate, send love—whatever practice moves you. Just understand the deeper truth: When you are whole and complete within yourself, giving happens naturally. It just flows out of you, and that is what blesses the world.

23-7.q: Can belief in God be rationally established in the mind, or is it to be experienced beyond the mind?
23-7.a:
You are correct that the mind cannot understand God, and it won’t help to keep thinking about it. The mind wants to know and understand what God is, so it does what the mind does best: it builds beliefs, concepts, and ideas, all based on our past experiences. But our past experiences don’t include Godrealization, so what can we do?

All the great ones from all religions have taught that God is everything that is, was, and ever will be. Fortunately, you do not have to use your mind to either believe or not believe in God. You can simply work on relaxing and releasing whenever your personal thoughts come up, and then focus on who is aware of the thoughts. You are in there, noticing the mind talking about everything. You are even noticing the mind talking about God! Keep relaxing when the personal mind is busy talking, as well as when you feel emotional reactions, and you will begin to experience a beautiful, silent clarity that is far beyond the mind.

The seat of consciousness is the core of your being—it is your soul, and it can directly experience its connection to God. This experience is far beyond the mind’s belief structure. Yet it naturally exists when the noise of the personal mind is no longer distracting you. When you interact with life from this place of deep clarity, you will find yourself living in a constant state of joy and love. Once you stop listening to the personal, it all becomes spiritual, and you will naturally feel your connection with Divinity. You will not have to think about it—you will be experiencing it.

23-8.q: They say God is love. Is that true, and can I experience that directly?
23-8.a:
There are many different levels of love. The love that is experienced as need is a human emotion caused by the heart being blocked to the inner flow of shakti. When the heart is unconditionally open, you will never feel the need for love because your heart will remain full of love regardless of what is happening. Such an open heart is difficult for people to achieve because they have stored pain from the past that creates blockages to the inner energy flow. This is why people often need special outside conditions in order for their heart to open. Let’s call that human love. It is still beautiful, especially compared to the other human emotions, but it is conditional, and it can create dependencies and attachments.

Spiritual love is very different. Once the heart learns to remain open, even under difficult circumstances, the flow of unhampered energy through the heart feeds the indwelling soul directly. Because you are now fulfilled inside, you don’t have to constantly control the outside. You are deeply content experiencing the inner flow of love.

Eventually, you will want to explore the source of this beautiful energy. The only way to explore the source is by falling into it. When you do so, you will become completely immersed in overwhelming love, joy, and bliss. This is the point where the shakti flow changes direction. You will begin to feel a tremendous upward flow pulling you beyond your sense of individuality. It feels like God is calling you home. And that is exactly what is happening.

The great ones have let go completely, and their drop of consciousness has merged back into the ocean of consciousness. This is Christ’s “I and my Father are one.” This is Buddha’s Nirvana. This is Islam’s Sufi Fanā, the complete dissolution of the ego/self in the presence of God. This is the Jewish Kabbalah’s Bitul HaYesh, dissolving the ego/self into Divine nothingness.

This is Enlightenment—the meaning of all of life.
